#176560. Breaking: U.S. court clears the way for Army’s planned ammunition detonation in Iowa

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (447 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: U.S. court clears the way for Army’s planned ammunition detonation in Iowa

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (447 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • appeals court on Monday cleared the Army to proceed with a controlled detonation of nearly five tons of degraded explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant, overturning a bid by environmental groups to block an emergency federal permit for the blast.
  • The order clears the way for the Army's initiative to destroy around 68 barrels of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, near the Iowa-Illinois border, on Wednesday.
  • Circuit Court of Appeals denied a request by environmental groups seeking to challenge an emergency permit from the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A U.S. appeals court on Monday cleared the Army to proceed with a controlled detonation of nearly five tons of degraded explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant, overturning a bid by environmental groups to block an emergency federal permit for the blast.

The order clears the way for the Army's initiative to destroy around 68 barrels of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, near the Iowa-Illinois border, on Wednesday.

A three-judge panel of the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied a request by environmental groups seeking to challenge an emergency permit from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency authorizing the operation.

According to recent reports, "We are mindful of the very real risks presented by the Army's planned detonation of the stores of degraded lead azide," the ruling mentioned. "However, we must acknowledge the realities of the situation: the degraded explosives present a risk of an uncontrolled and unplanned explosion, which would occur without the benefit of the safety measures that the Permit puts in place.".

The planned blast, originally scheduled for Nov. 20, has been delayed three times amid regional concerns over possible health and environmental effects and criticism that the government failed to adequately communicate the potential risks to local communities.

The detonation is expected to produce a dust plume containing lead particles, a toxic metal that can cause serious health effects, according to the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services. Breathing in lead-containing particles or coming into contact with lead dust deposited on surrounding surfaces could pose potential health risks, the agency mentioned.

The U.S. Army has argued that the risk of the material detonating on its own has increased as temperatures fall, and that the explosive compound, stored for more than two decades, has degraded to the point that moving it is too dangerous.

President Donald Trump mentioned in a social media post Monday that he had told the Army to hold off until the court weighed in. He added that the decision would be subject to Iowa's Democratic Gov.-elect Rob Sand, who takes office in January, warning that further delay could risk "a large, spontaneous explosion.".

In an X post late Monday following the court ruling, Sand said the Trump administration "should make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks.".

"Everyday Iowans are entitled to know how Middletown came to this situation, and learn why the administration believes this is the best path forward," Sand said, urging the federal government to share information with the public as soon as possible.

#176557. Latest Update: Quitting can actually be the key to success, states expert: It's one of the 'most courageous moves you can make'

Latest Update: Quitting can actually be the key to success, states expert: It's one of the 'most courageous moves you can make'

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lindsay Crouse wants people to stop treating "quitter" like a bad word.
  • In fact, the former New York Times journalist believes that knowing when to quit is a crucial component to a successful, healthy life.
  • In a recent development, but Crouse didn't always feel that way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lindsay Crouse wants people to stop treating "quitter" like a bad word.

In fact, the former New York Times journalist believes that knowing when to quit is a crucial component to a successful, healthy life.

In a recent development, but Crouse didn't always feel that way. In her recent book "The Case for Quitting: The Surprising Benefits of Opting Out," published in September, Crouse shared that she used to push herself to the point of exhaustion at work and as a distance runner and marathoner.

"I'd achieved things I'd never dreamed were in reach, yet it didn't feel like enough. I was doing too much, and somehow it amounted to less than before," she wrote.

Industry observers note that now, Crouse wants to challenge the popular narrative around quitting. She spoke to psychologists, endurance athletes and fellow recovering workaholics about what they gained when they decided to let go.

Sources indicate that "We're conditioned to see perseverance and quitting in these very binary ways," she tells CNBC Make It. "We think of people who never give up as people who succeed, and people who quit as people who fail.".

But in Crouse's view, quitting can actually be a strategic move that allows us to focus on what's vital.

"If we're going to succeed and do our very best, we need to learn to walk away," she indicates. "We need to learn to abandon paths that aren't working in order to find paths that might succeed.".

When you're already struggling with something, "it's really natural to want to escalate your commitment to achieving your goal," Crouse notes.

That could mean putting even more hours into a job that you know deep down isn't a good fit for you, or pushing yourself harder during marathon training because you're frustrated by an injury slowing you down.

But what many people don't realize is that investing more energy into a failing cause "actually only creates more failure," she says.

In those cases, doggedly persevering only "increases the amount that you lose, whether that's energy, whether it's money, whether it's time, or whether it's just your happiness," she indicates. "If you don't cut your losses, those losses are only going to grow.".

To determine whether your approach to a task is becoming "a little unhealthy," Crouse recommends asking yourself these questions:.

Recent findings suggest that "How are you talking about achieving your goal? Are you getting more and more desperate? Are you constantly telling yourself that success is just one beat away, even as evidence might be telling you otherwise?".

If the answer is "yes" to the latter two questions, it might be a sign that you need to take a step back and reevaluate whether it makes sense to keep pushing — or whether it's time to pivot, Crouse says.

It can also be helpful to ask your friends whether they think you're on the right track, she says: "A lot of times, our friends will tell us the truth that we don't want to hear.".

If you still feel like quitting is a sign of failure, Crouse recommends looking at it from a different angle.

Quitting is "one of the most courageous moves you can make," she says, because it "inherently involves risk, and being brave enough to do it means that you have confidence that you can look at something uncertain, take it on and make it work out.".

Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (446 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
  • Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively latest corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
  • Sources indicate that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively latest corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

Sources indicate that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

According to recent reports, securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

It has been revealed that securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The tech giant posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and confirmed the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo remarked.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 11:37 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • In a recent development, derek McInnes can be understood in wanting a quiet January window.
    • In the case of Olwethu Makhanya, for example, this is definitely not the time to sell.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 11:37 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 20 November 2026.

    In a recent development, derek McInnes can be understood in wanting a quiet January window. He’s still bonding a squad of players together. Drama and diversions are the last thing he needs when there looks to be an opportunity to win a title on the horizon.

    In the case of Olwethu Makhanya, for example, this is definitely not the time to sell.

    The 22-year-old South African has been impressive at centre-back, but it will take a campaign catching the attention in high-level European football for him to raise his value to Calvin Bassey levels and beyond.

    Same goes for the likes of Ryan Naderi. Getting into the Czechia squad and increasing his range of experience makes him a more interesting prospect, but UEFA competition is a platform that ought to increase his premium.

    In a recent development, mcInnes, as he did this week, has to say he wants to keep his more prominent talents anyway. It would be strange to appear accepting of the board cashing in on bigger players.

    When it comes to Nico Raskin, however, things are different. A buyer for him should have been found in the summer after his World Cup involvement with Belgium.

    Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin is an asset who could be sold in the January transfer window.

    From the chit-chat around the game, it does not seem unreasonable to think Rangers maybe overvalued him in the initial part of that window and missed the boat in terms of securing a sale.

    If he stays for the rest of this season and enters the final year of his contract, though, the money you can ask for naturally reduces. The club might seek to tie him up on a new deal, of course, but his remarks about being ‘mentally ready to leave’ at the start of the season point to the most likely direction of travel.

    Recent findings suggest that is he irreplaceable? Not at all. And this is where forward planning should come into the mix.

    If there’s someone out there willing to edge anywhere close to the £15m mark for the 25-year-old, they should be getting sounded out now – with a contingency strategy being discussed and worked on in tandem.

    Yes, Rangers need to get back to winning silverware, but the need to start raising funds through selling players – and replacing them - at appropriate times is pressing too.

    As often said here, they can’t keep spending money the way they have been without considerably more coming back in return.

    Industry observers note that raskin’s a good player, but his three-and-a-half years at Ibrox have hardly been shaped by his propensity for winning medals, have they? If a realistic fee is there in January, there’s a case to make for it being taken.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Upcoming York Federal Reserve President John Williams said Monday that policymakers have more work to do to bring inflation under control, though he indicated that further action can unfold over time as the economy continues to grow.

    In remarks consistent with previous statements, the influential central banker expressed confidence that inflation will get closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027 before hitting the goal the following year. He also said that while artificial intelligence is pressuring prices, there's "little evidence" it will be the source of more persistent inflation.

    According to recent reports, "But getting inflation back to 2% is 100% essential," he noted in remarks at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in Fresh York. "We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis. There is still work to do to get that done.".

    The comments come at a delicate moment for monetary policy, as the economy continues to grow and inflation stays well above the Fed's goal.

    Fed officials have differed over how quickly to raise rates, with some advocating more aggressive action while others, including Williams, have emphasized a measured approach.

    Williams ascribed the current inflation pressures to the conflict in Iran, demand for goods associated with the AI build-out and tariffs, the effects of which he said "have largely abated" as a source of pressure. Nevertheless, he expressed confidence that inflation will subside substantially in 2027 even as economic growth remains robust and unemployment edges lower.

    It has been revealed that the Federal Open Market Committee next meets on Dec. 8-9, with markets fully pricing in a quarter percentage point interest rate increase from the current target range of 3.75%-4%. The remarks from Williams are expected to be the last major policy statement from any Fed official before the December decision.

    "Monetary policy cannot move ships or reopen pipelines and refineries, but it can — and must — ensure that these shocks do not lead to broader or persistent inflationary dynamics or erode well-anchored inflation expectations," Williams said, according to his prepared remarks.

    Williams did not explicitly address the December meeting expectations, instead pointing to the statement released after the prior FOMC meeting in late October that said the "accumulation of more information" will help decide the future policy path.

    "The data that we have received since then show that the economy has remained strong and that inflation has continued to run too high," he said.

    Industry News: Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

    • Industry observers note that there was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that there was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

    Recent findings suggest that everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

    If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

    Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a significant night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

    Sources indicate that poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

    It has been revealed that “With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”.

    So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

    A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

    How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his latest territory.

    It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

    Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

    He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

    According to recent reports, iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

    Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

    “I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

    Sources indicate that what damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

    Sources indicate that the next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

    Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

    It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

    In a recent development, inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

    “He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

    A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

    Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

    There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

    Industry observers note that “I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The vital thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”.

    "My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS.

    Sources indicate that “He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”.

    "Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw.

    “We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

    “It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”.

    We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

    The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

    In a recent development, andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

    “We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola noted. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

    “He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”.

    Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

    It has been revealed that ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

    It has been revealed that “What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil stated. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”.

    Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.
    • The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.
    • The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola stated afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

    The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

    The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola stated afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

    The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

    However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

    The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

    ‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

    Recent findings suggest that the incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

    Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

    It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

    Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.

    Welcome to our Live Comments section, where fresh comments will appear automatically.

    #176541. Peterson: Here’s what Bessent’s about-face on Jensen Huang reveals about Trump and China

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (898 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Peterson: Here’s what Bessent’s about-face on Jensen Huang reveals about Trump and China

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For a minute there, it seemed like someone in the Trump administration might actually be willing to stand up to China.
    • It has been revealed that for about a week and a half, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia over the potential risks its co-founder Jensen Huang's affairs posed to national security.
    • Sources indicate that they see China's AI program as a major threat, and want to restrain its growth by cutting off the supply of advanced chips to China.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For a minute there, it seemed like someone in the Trump administration might actually be willing to stand up to China.

    It has been revealed that for about a week and a half, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia over the potential risks its co-founder Jensen Huang's affairs posed to national security. Bessent was giving voice to China hawks who had felt sidelined by the Trump administration's willingness to sell artificial intelligence chips to  China.

    Sources indicate that they see China's AI program as a major threat, and want to restrain its growth by cutting off the supply of advanced chips to China. The resignation of Huang, who pressed the Trump Administration to allow the exports, seemed to signal that the hawks had found fresh influence in Washington.

    By this weekend, Bessent had softened his public resistance to Huang's reinstatement. That came just in time for Nvidia's board to reappoint Huang as CEO at President Donald Trump's urging.

    Industry observers note that whether any real damage was done to national security isn't clear. But it is safe to say that the incoming Democratic majority in Congress won't take Trump at his word when he mentioned on CNBC Monday that the Department of Justice "did a pretty good investigation" that exonerated Huang.

    Congress will look deeply into the worries Bessent himself raised about Huang's acknowledged romantic relationship with a woman The New York Times and others have reported was a Chinese intelligence asset.

    Nvidia's board noted it had received assurances from top U.S. officials and had concluded his return wasn't a national security risk.

    Sources indicate that A top concern is whether China was able to use the affair to help divert Nvidia's high-end artificial intelligence chips toward helping its military. Bessent in a Nov. 13 interview with CNBC outlined the stakes.

    "Any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts the — it hurts our great companies and in the AI race it gives the Chinese an advantage," he mentioned.

    Bessent said that his department and others had wanted to blacklist Megaspeed, the organization previously run by Alice Huang, Jensen Huang's paramour. But "Commerce has the pen," Bessent said.

    The Commerce Department is headed by Secretary Howard Lutnick, Bessent's rival.

    Putting Huang back at Nvidia wasn't originally Bessent's preference. He mentioned in a Fox interview on Nov. 15 that the board should "go outside the organization" to find a upcoming leader. But by this past weekend, Bessent had apparently gotten on board with Trump's wishes.

    "Jensen is on the outside now," Bessent told CBS on Sunday, in trying to explain his apparent policy shift.

    Sources indicate that commerce has since taken steps to tighten some restrictions meant to prevent U.S. chips from helping China advance in the AI race.

    But there is bipartisan worry about the Nvidia episode. "I think we need to catalog the damage that's been done," Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., told The Wall Street Journal. He mentioned Lutnick had not responded to letters he sent saying the administration should be "taking the threats of communist China more seriously.".

    Recent findings suggest that but Trump has clearly put an upper limit on how aggressively anyone in his administration can push back on China. The president said Monday that he was swayed by the pageantry in his visit to China last week.

    Xi "met me at the plane, which is something they've never done, which was a sign," Trump stated.

    Trump remarked he felt like he needed to intervene to back Huang because the stock market was plummeting in the wake of Nvidia's troubles — a development he also blamed on Democrats' midterm victory.

    In a recent development, "I watched our country lose $5 trillion because of a bad election," he said. "If I didn't get involved, you'd probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come." Now, its stock performance will be "unbelievable.".

    According to recent reports, bessent on Sunday played down the market risks. The organization "continues to be fantastically profitable, and there is near unlimited demand for their chips worldwide," he told CBS.

    According to recent reports, lutnick has embraced Trump's transactional urges. He has backed deals in which the U.S. takes equity stakes in companies such as Intel, saying the taxpayer deserves some of the upside.

    Lutnick in January mentioned he had heard Huang pitch Trump on allowing Nvidia to sell its relatively more advanced H200 chips into China.

    "There are strong — two sides. We shouldn't sell them any or we should sell them." Where does he stand? "Right in the middle," Lutnick told Bloomberg. Trump decided to go ahead with the deal.

    Recent findings suggest that bessent has noted he is "neither a hawk nor a dove" on China, and is simply trying to manage the ultra-sensitive relationship between the world's two biggest economies. But the upshot of the Huang affair seems to be that Bessent wasn't able to sway the president on a matter that seemed cut-and-dried just days ago.

    Lutnick, meanwhile, is riding high.

    Recent findings suggest that trump remarked he discussed whether Huang should return to Nvidia with Lutnick, Bessent and Vice President JD Vance. "Howard Lutnick was very good. Very, he's very professional," Trump said on CNBC Monday.

    "I call them the opposites, Scott and Howard," Trump added, before declaring them "both good.".

    #176540. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (748 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer.
    • It has been revealed that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the manufacturer. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    It has been revealed that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the organization to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    According to recent reports, tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    Sources indicate that on Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    In a recent development, it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The tech giant had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    According to recent reports, coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, mentioned CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he mentioned.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my tech giant every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real issue is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    Recent findings suggest that "Substantial companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he stated. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Russia's Foreign Ministry has lashed out at Estonia's government, accusing the NATO member of carrying out a range of "hostile actions" and putting the Baltic state "on the verge of unleashing open war" with Moscow.
    • Recent findings suggest that the outburst underscores rising tensions between Russia and countries on NATO's eastern flank and comes after Estonia revealed it will close its road border crossings with Russia from Dec.
    • Russia's ministry said Monday it had lodged a formal protest to Estonia's chargé d'affaires, Marek Uhtegi, over Tallinn's decision to close its border crossings and accused the European Union member of imposing a naval blockade against Moscow.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Russia's Foreign Ministry has lashed out at Estonia's government, accusing the NATO member of carrying out a range of "hostile actions" and putting the Baltic state "on the verge of unleashing open war" with Moscow.

    Recent findings suggest that the outburst underscores rising tensions between Russia and countries on NATO's eastern flank and comes after Estonia revealed it will close its road border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1.

    Russia's ministry said Monday it had lodged a formal protest to Estonia's chargé d'affaires, Marek Uhtegi, over Tallinn's decision to close its border crossings and accused the European Union member of imposing a naval blockade against Moscow.

    "The Estonian diplomat was again informed that such provocative and extremely dangerous actions are on the verge of unleashing open war with Russia," the ministry said in a statement, describing measures taken by Estonian lawmakers as "Russophobic.".

    The ministry also accused Estonia of "tacitly" providing its airspace for Ukrainian drone flights and sharply criticized Tallinn's ban on the transit of Russian and Belarusian grain through Estonian territory, referring to a policy that was introduced at the start of October.

    Estonia, which shares a 294-kilometer (183-mile) border with Russia, swiftly denied ever allowing its territory to be used for military operations by another country.

    It also responded to Russia's allegations by saying the Kremlin appears to be seeking to divert attention from its own efforts to undermine European security.

    "Russian missiles have reached Polish territory, Danish security services have identified an assassination plot in Denmark orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, merchant vessels in the Black Sea are under constant threat from Russian attacks, and in Estonia, an arson attack targeting a defence industry firm, planned on the orders of Russian military intelligence, was foiled," Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated Monday.

    "All this is happening while Russia continues its war of aggression against Ukraine," he added.

    Recent findings suggest that the rhetoric marks a significant escalation in tensions between Estonia and Russia. Tallinn, a staunch Ukraine ally, has frequently raised the alarm over sabotage attacks against NATO countries that have been supporting Kyiv since Russia launched the full-scale invasion of its neighbor in February 2022.

    In a recent development, earlier this month, Estonia said it would close road border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1 as it blames Moscow for an attempted "sabotage" of one of its defense companies, an allegation the Kremlin denies.

    Tallinn has stated the border closure will help to reduce Moscow's ability to conduct hostile activities against it and mitigate risks related to sanctions circumvention.

    Ukraine has stepped up its attacks on Russian critical targets in recent weeks, damaging Russian President Vladimir Putin's prized Crimea bridge, striking a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea and destroying one of Russia's newest ships at a Libyan port.

    The suspected Ukrainian attack on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday prompted Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo to warn that the Ukraine war is "spilling over" into its immediate vicinity.

    Finland, one of NATO's newest members, has also closed its land border crossings with Russia.

    Ukraine's latest attacks on some of Russia's most protected targets have demonstrated Kyiv's capabilities to hurt Moscow even without ample U.S. military support, according to Mario Bikarski, senior Europe and Central Asia analyst for Verisk Maplecroft, a political risk consultancy.

    "Ukraine will continue to look for ways to degrade not only Russia's economy, but also its geostrategic interests in the wider region, including the Mediterranean and the Middle East," Bikarski said.

    The prospect of an imminent peace deal between Russia and Ukraine appears to be slim, Bikarski said, although "the latest surge in diplomatic activity and mounting losses for both sides signals an appetite from all sides to reach an agreement.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia shares fell around 8% on Tuesday, paring a massive Monday rally that was sparked by the return of Jensen Huang as CEO.

    It has been revealed that other U.S. semiconductor stocks also opened lower after posting strong increases Monday. Micron declined 11%, Marvell Technology lost nearly 10%, Arm Holdings dropped over 9% and AMD shed 12% in morning trading.

    Neoclouds also gave back some of their Monday gains, with CoreWeave losing over 13%, Iren declining 15% and Nebius shedding 13%.

    Recent findings suggest that huang, who resigned as CEO of Nvidia earlier this month after admitting to an extramarital affair, was reinstated on Monday. The stock closed over 30% higher following the news of Huang's return.

    The manufacturer's board of directors stated it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.

    President Donald Trump also claimed he was personally involved in Huang's return. The president told CNBC that he spoke with the chipmaker's board before it reversed course and reinstated its co-founder.

    "I made the deal," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers on Monday during an interview on "Squawk on the Street.".

    Trump mentioned Nvidia's board asked for guarantees that Huang, who resigned less than two weeks ago, was not a threat to national security.

    Recent findings suggest that "And we gave them assurances, at least with everything we know," the president noted. "We believe he's fine. He's absolutely fine.".

    After Huang's reinstatement, several Wall Street analysts turned more bullish on the stock and upgraded their ratings on Nvidia.

    "We believe reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang RETURNS Investor CONFIDENCE in the AI trade," Mizuho analysts wrote in a note on Monday.

    Huang and Nvidia have been central to the AI story, supplying the chips that power AI and financing companies across the ecosystem.

    The tech giant remains under scrutiny as questions remain about Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy.

    In a recent development, the U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed, the tech giant where she worked. Questions also remain regarding whether Nvidia chips are making their way into China despite export controls.

    In a recent development, huang is set to publicly testify in front of the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to take over the Committee in January, called Huang's reinstatement "reckless.".

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Warren remarked in a statement on Monday.

    Huang is also expected to sit for a closed-door interview with the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select committees on Dec. 1.

    Sources indicate that "Reinstatement should not be confused with the end of scrutiny," Bank of America said in a note on Monday. "We therefore expect elevated attention around governance, China/export controls, customer relationships and compliance to persist even with the CEO question resolved.".

    — CNBC's Luke Fountain, Seema Mody and Dan Mangan contributed to this report.

    Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved in any wrongdoing at his former club Manchester City – but refused to rule out taking action against them if their appeal fails.

    According to recent reports, in his first sit-down interview in five months, broadcast on Friday, Berrada tackled a range of topics concerning United but his links to City, from whom he joined United in 2024, were also brought up. He worked at the club during some of the period that City were found to have broken Premier League rules.

    Back in September, an independent regulatory commission found City guilty of a multitude of charges brought against them by the Premier League, with financial offences ranging between 2009 and 2018.

    The scathing verdict determined that City had 'artificially inflated' their revenues and reduced costs through 'disguised funding' schemes such as 'sham' contracts.

    Berrada joined City in 2011 before going on to become their chief operating officer in 2016, raising questions over whether he could end up implicated if City – who vehemently contest the charges – fail in their appeal.

    Sources indicate that 'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted. 'I want to be very clear about this, right. I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings; there are no allegations against me, and in that sense there will be no surprises.'.

    Asked if United would push for compensation should City's guilty verdict be upheld on appeal, Berrada remained tight-lipped.

    Recent findings suggest that omar Berrada joined Manchester City in 2011... and moved across the city 13 years later.

    Berrada has become one of the main sources of anger among United fans who have campaigned against the owners and the board.

    In a recent development, 'I don't want to comment on that because right now it's an ongoing process,' he added. 'When it runs its course we'll take our view of where is our position as Manchester United.'.

    Berrada was not used as a witness in the original investigation and there are no allegations directed specifically to the now-United CEO.

    City boss Enzo Maresca, meanwhile, insisted that the guilty verdicts handed down to Manchester City for financial chicanery have not affected his players despite three consecutive Premier League defeats.

    City fell six points behind defending champions Arsenal in the weeks before this month’s international break amid a slew of individual high-profile errors that led to claims of Maresca’s squad being preoccupied by the uncertainty surrounding the club.

    The Premier League have a range of available sanctions to them were City to lose an appeal set for next month. Those would likely result in relegation to the Championship.

    But Maresca does not equate that looming doomsday backdrop with a worrying run of form before they face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday lunchtime.

    ‘I don't think the players are thinking too much about that,’ Maresca stated. ‘If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, look at [Aston] Villa away. We had so many chances, for instance Iliman [Ndiaye] hit the post, or Brighton where the keeper was man of the match.

    Enzo Maresca insists his stars are not thinking about the impact of the guilty verdict.

    Erling Haaland notes he is 'incredibly' happy to be a City player and tops the Premier League scoring charts with nine so far this campaign.

    ‘Then [Nottingham] Forest when Erling [Haaland] had the chance to score for 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise. I don't think they are worried about that.’.

    Haaland claimed to be ‘incredibly happy’ about being a City player in a defiant interview with Norwegian television earlier in the week, although few others have addressed the problems publicly.

    Marc Guehi has previously said the players are ‘relaxed’, while Phil Foden refused to discuss it when asked.

    Maresca has spent the past fortnight analysing City’s ten league matches and has admitted that the team requires more balance after conceding too many goals to turnovers or counter attacks.

    ‘I was not thinking that we were doing everything well when we were winning games and I'm not thinking that we did everything wrong when we lost games,’ the Italian added.

    ‘For me it is the beginning of something long. I think we are attacking well because we are creating chances and overall we are controlling games.

    ‘There are moments we are not controlling and we have to realise the reasons why and do better. We are conceding goals and most are avoidable from my point of view.’.

    There have been occasions – like the first goal at Forest – when City’s building from the back has put them in serious trouble. Josko Gvardiol lost the ball at the City Ground after no midfielder had shown for possession.

    It has been revealed that maresca remarked: ‘We reviewed things during the break. The idea is to continue to attack in the same way and try to find the balance when we defend or when we are building like what happened for the first goal against Forest.

    ‘When you are building and you lose the ball in the build-up it's difficult to build with that.’.

    • Recent findings suggest that nvidia finance chief Colette Kress led the tech giant for 11 days during Jensen Huang's sudden but brief departure.
    • The 59-year-old Kress at the moment has roughly 4.775 million shares directly and indirectly held, which makes her worth approximately $778 million at Monday's market close.
    • The 63-year-old Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital relationships, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia finance chief Colette Kress led the tech giant for 11 days during Jensen Huang's sudden but brief departure. When Nvidia's board officially reinstated Huang as CEO on Monday, the company also announced that Kress would continue in her role as CFO.

    The 59-year-old Kress at the moment has roughly 4.775 million shares directly and indirectly held, which makes her worth approximately $778 million at Monday's market close.

    The 63-year-old Huang resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital relationships, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy.

    Nvidia stock soared 31% and the Nasdaq surged more than 6% Monday after the firm announced that Huang would return as CEO, president and board director, effective immediately. Huang returned to the office Monday to crowds of Nvidia employees cheering his return.

    Kress, who stepped in as interim CEO during Nvidia's moment of crisis, joined the chipmaker as finance chief in September 2013 following stints at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments.

    As CFO, Kress oversees the balance sheet of a tech giant aggressively financing many of the infrastructure deals that power the artificial intelligence buildout. Those agreements also raise concerns over circular financing and Nvidia's AI exposure in the event of a slowdown.

    In the first earnings call after Huang's resignation, Kress sought to reassure investors, raising the company's fiscal 2028 revenue-growth forecast to roughly 75% from 70%.

    In a recent development, she told analysts during a Q&A portion that it was "business as usual" at the company. She later told CNBC's Jim Cramer that customers have stood by the chipmaker and that demand continues increasing.

    "The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen, and that is our statement and what the board has decided to do," Kress remarked.

    During the organization's first all-hands meeting after Huang's resignation, Kress also struck an optimistic tone, telling employees to "move forward" and mentioning pay raises.

    But Kress didn't manage to impress many market participants and insiders, who compared the interim chief to Huang. Last week, the stock recorded its worst week and longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis as AI stocks plummeted.

    It has been revealed that "She just wasn't him," The Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman told CNBC. "I think she would have had to strengthen her bench around her a lot, because you have a visionary, product technology driven CEO that was literally the epicenter of the company. He was the entire identity.".

    One person CNBC spoke with mentioned Kress handled the situation with "skill and grace" while managing a tough job.

    The former Nvidia employee, who asked not to be named because the matter is private, remarked Kress helped reassure the industry and that people should not be so "quick to rush to judgment.".

    In the week since Huang's exit, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang belittled Kress, calling her "a deer in the headlights.".

    Huang said in the press release announcing his return that he was "grateful" for Kress "leading NVIDIA during this period.".

    "I think she is a fantastic CFO. I think Jensen probably has great confidence in her. I hope she stays," the former Nvidia employee said. "I don't think that she's going to be on thin ice when Jensen returns.".

    Nvidia did not immediately respond to comment for this story.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Members of Congress from both parties on Monday expressed outrage and incredulity, and doubled down on their calls for investigations, after Nvidia declared it has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO.

    The resurrection of Huang, who had resigned from the artificial intelligence behemoth just 11 days earlier, raises more questions about the company's decision-making and the Trump administration's national security assessments, on top of existing concerns about Nvidia's advanced AI chips being diverted to China, the lawmakers said.

    "It's inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO," Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a China hawk who is retiring from Congress, told CNBC in a phone interview. "To me it's a failure of character.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC in an extended interview later Monday morning that he personally intervened to convince Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, saying, "I made the deal.".

    Bacon, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation, noted he wants the next Congress to conduct thorough oversight, while questioning the Trump administration's motives.

    Sources indicate that "Somebody's responsible for this, and it may be" Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose department is responsible for setting U.S. export controls on AI chips, Bacon stated. "But I think we should get to the bottom of this.".

    It has been revealed that huang, who is scheduled to testify before multiple committees on Capitol Hill starting Dec. 1, is "going to get high scrutiny in a bipartisan way when he comes next week," Bacon noted.

    Huang's closed-door appearance before a trio of House committees is on the schedule, as the panels seek answers on the national security implications of Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, MS NOW reported. The Senate banking committee announced after Huang's reinstatement that he will appear for a public hearing Dec. 3.

    John Fisher of Trident, a spokesman for Huang, declined to comment on the Nvidia CEO's scheduled appearances.

    "He better be there," Rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told CNBC about Huang's scheduled Dec. 1 appearance. His reinstatement will only intensify congressional probes into Nvidia and its government connections, Amo predicted.

    "I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query, and it makes Howard Lutnick and his dealings — supporting his nepo children's operation at Cantor Fitzgerald — party to inquiry as well as any other administration official that has facilitated a status quo in which chips can be sold to China or Chinese operated intermediaries who don't intend good things for the American people," remarked Amo, referring to the financial firm run by Lutnick's sons that has business ties to Nvidia.

    A Cantor spokesperson didn't comment directly when asked about Amo's comments, saying the firm "holds no material proprietary position in Nvidia" and noting its Nvidia positions "arise primarily from equity swaps executed for clients.".

    The Commerce Department didn't immediately respond to requests to comment on Bacon's and Amo's remarks.

    Nvidia in a statement Monday mentioned it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    Industry observers note that david Rudenstine, a constitutional law professor and national security scholar at Cardozo School of Law, stated the frenzy around Huang's comeback is secondary to lingering national security concerns."The real responsibility for national security is with the administration and not with the CEO of a private company," Rudenstine told CNBC."You're opposed to China getting the chips. You recognize that the intermediary companies are sending chips to China, and you don't put a stop to it. I don't get it," he said.

    The CEO's reinstatement, while celebrated by the White House and in Silicon Valley, led to heightened calls on Capitol Hill to seek answers on AI chip exports to China and what the Trump administration's role has been in facilitating that.

    Industry observers note that "We are sending high-end computer chips to China, and yet we're saying we want to win the AI war. It's a contradiction, and it's a failure of leadership in the White House," Bacon told CNBC.

    Industry observers note that sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon, the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee, told CNBC in an emailed statement that Huang's return "proves that under Trump, Vance, and Rubio, national security is for sale to the highest bidder.".

    Industry observers note that "We will all pay the price of letting China plunder America's cutting edge technology. Democrats will be pushing for accountability for anyone in the administration that put corrupt deals over our country's security," Wyden, who is also a Senate Intelligence Committee member, remarked.

    Trump in a Truth Social post Monday added that Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    Lawmakers, who have already rolled out multiple investigations related to Huang, Nvidia and related entities, quickly filed in to question those conclusions.

    Recent findings suggest that sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., a close Trump ally and a former CEO, criticized the move and called for a congressional briefing "as soon as possible" on Huang's reinstatement.

    Industry observers note that "Nvidia's board is free to vote however they want, but the federal government owes the American people answers about what actually happened," Scott told CNBC in an emailed statement. "This looks terrible on its face, and it drives home the need for Congress to be informed on the full impact of Jensen Huang's actions on our national security and economy.".

    Rep. Scott Peters, D-Calif., a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, told CNBC that it's still not clear to what degree Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy might have compromised national security.

    "The fact that the president of the United States is involved in putting him back in there, presumably because maybe he has stock or he just cares about the stock market, it's really reached a bizarre place," Peters said. "And obviously that man has not learned anything from the election about what people think of him, or he doesn't care.".

    Monday's move also gave fuel to lawmakers who have already questioned Trump, his administration or Nvidia.

    According to recent reports, "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., noted in a statement via the Senate Banking Committee, where she is the top Democrat and is expected to become chair in January.

    Industry observers note that sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, more tersely questioned the official assurances that Huang poses no risks to national security.

    Sources indicate that "No national security risk? Based on what?" he wrote on X.

    Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-Ill., who serves on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, in an X post called Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang "outrageous.".

    "We still don't know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia's own board has completed its investigation," wrote Krishnamoorthi, who is also a member of the House Oversight and Intelligence panels.

    — CNBC's Dan Mangan, Garrett Downs and Luke Fountain contributed to this report.

    The NFL is taking over Thanksgiving. But how much football is too much football?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1064 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that you know how Thursday's going to go, right?
    • In a recent development, I'm talking about your NFL diet, of course, but you'll probably do the same thing with turkey, too.
    • It has been revealed that the NFL has honed its Thanksgiving Day slate into a sleek, efficient set-your-oven-timer tradition.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that you know how Thursday's going to go, right? You're going to load up your plate and feast, you're going to take a moment to catch your breath, you're going to dive back in for more, you're going to grab a quick nap, and then after the sun goes down you're going to go back for one more helping.

    In a recent development, I'm talking about your NFL diet, of course, but you'll probably do the same thing with turkey, too. And as with turkey leftovers, there'll come a point when you realize that the fifth helping isn't nearly as much fun as the first.

    It has been revealed that the NFL has honed its Thanksgiving Day slate into a sleek, efficient set-your-oven-timer tradition. You'll watch the Lions, a team that's finally fun to watch instead of being the equivalent of Thanksgiving green bean casserole. You'll watch the inescapable Cowboys, once again almost ready to make a run. And you'll try to stay awake for the evening game. (You will fail.).

    It's been this way since 1934, when the Lions began playing on Thanksgiving; since 1966, when the Cowboys joined them; and since 2006, when the league added the third game. Every year, before a captive holiday audience, these games do numbers; last year's Chiefs-Cowboys game was the most-watched NFL regular-season game in history.

    And now, with Thanksgiving firmly in hand, the NFL is looking to run up the score. Three years ago, the league rolled out a Black Friday game kicking off midafternoon, so you'll have something to watch as you scroll through sale after sale. This year, the Shield is planting the flag on another spot: Thanksgiving Eve.

    Traditionally the province of impromptu high school reunions and travel nightmares, the night before Thanksgiving will now host an NFL game. This year, the Packers will play the Rams on Netflix while you're running around trying to see if you bought yams and figuring out how to defrost a frozen-solid 20-pound turkey in just a few hours. And that's just the start of the NFL turkey festivities.

    Sources indicate that on Thanksgiving Day, the Lions will play the Bears, and then we'll all try to keep our dinner down as the Eagles play the Cowboys. The evening game will feature one of the best matchups of the year — Chiefs-Bills — and Friday, the Broncos will meet the Steelers. (Even though literally any game would do numbers on Thanksgiving, the NFL is showing some mercy. They've stashed Jets-Dolphins — a game more unhealthy than undercooked turkey — on Sunday rather than exposing America to those kinds of toxins on a holiday.).

    Is all this football too much football? Depends on how you frame the question.

    According to recent reports, the holiday football format has held up like few other pop culture traditions in American life, from radio to television to cable to streaming. And it's based on a simple American truth: We would rather do anything than talk to our families.

    According to recent reports, OK, that's not quite accurate. It's theoretically possible to both watch football and talk to your family. Encouraged, even, considering how promptly family conversations can swing from friendly banter to open hostility. Long-simmering resentments, gossip, political disputes, in-law trouble, questioning of life choices … why throw open the doors to that furnace when everyone can come together and rail on the Cowboys defense?

    The league, so famous for owning Sundays, will broadcast games on five of six days starting on Wednesday.

    According to recent reports, there are two ways to look at this explosion of holiday football, from both the fan and the economic perspective. For the vast majority of Americans, the NFL's land grab — which also includes Christmas Eve and three games on Christmas Day — means that there are ever fewer hours when the NFL isn't demanding your attention.

    Industry observers note that as holiday problems go, "too much football" isn't exactly a terrible one. And hey, if that's what gets you through the holidays, no shame whatsoever. But isn't there something to be noted for a bit of peace and quiet, too? Maybe sitting by a fire, or catching up with friends and family, or watching an ungrateful Peppermint Patty crash Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving? There are millions of NFL fans whose lives would measurably improve if they weren't tying their emotional state to their team — you know the ones, I don't have to name them — so maybe give that a try for a couple hours?

    Which leads to the larger point: the more football we see, the less important each individual game becomes. For now, Mark Cuban's infamous prediction for the NFL — pigs get fat, hogs get slaughtered — still isn't anywhere close to truth; the league continues to fatten up, year after year. Maybe that'll change, maybe the arrow will flatten out instead of continuing to go up and to the right, but it hasn't yet.

    But popularity is context-dependent. The NFL is popular in part because of its scarcity; you wouldn't get eight-figure viewership levels for literally every single game if teams played, say, 162 of them in a season. The league, so famous for owning Sundays, will broadcast games on five of six days starting on Wednesday, and if you think the league doesn't have its eye on similar expansions throughout the season, we have a St. Louis Rams jersey to sell you.

    In a recent development, the NFL specializes in creating capital-E Events out of thin air. The Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix will boast fanfare literally worthy of a Super Bowl, including a halftime show featuring U2. The five Thanksgiving games will air on five different networks and services — Netflix, Fox, CBS, NBC and Prime — each with its own spectacle, its own flash-and-dazzle to catch and hold your attention through the holiday noise.

    We're getting perilously close to old-man-yells-at-turkey-leg territory here, but when everything is a spectacle, nothing is. Thanksgiving dinner — turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, et cetera — is so damn delicious because it comes around only once a year. But every week? Maybe not so much. Sometimes, you don't know how unique something is until it's everywhere.

    Recent findings suggest that enjoy Thanksgiving, friends, and enjoy the football. It'll all be worth watching. Yes, even Cowboys-Eagles.
