    #176527. Commercial real estate activity falls 14% in October, as interest rates rise

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (684 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Commercial real estate activity falls 14% in October, as interest rates rise

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Interest rates moved higher in September, and that had a swift impact on commercial real estate deal-making.
    • As a result, commercial real estate activity dropped 14% in October from September, according to an index from LightBox, a commercial real estate data platform.
    • Recent findings suggest that the appraisal measure is at its weakest level of the three and is now down 17% from a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Interest rates moved higher in September, and that had a swift impact on commercial real estate deal-making. After settling in the low-to-mid-4% range, the yield on the 10-year Treasury moved above 5% and has been wavering around there with the potential to move even higher due to stubborn inflation.

    As a result, commercial real estate activity dropped 14% in October from September, according to an index from LightBox, a commercial real estate data platform. Of the index's three components, commercial property listings fell 20% from September, environmental site assessments were down 1% and lender appraisals dropped 11%.

    Recent findings suggest that the appraisal measure is at its weakest level of the three and is now down 17% from a year ago. It demonstrates that both lenders and borrowers are stepping back, unable to pencil deals and move from listing to closing.

    It has been revealed that "What makes this so interesting is that during tariffs, it didn't dip. During $100 oil earlier this year, it didn't dip. When we saw interest rates marching up the first half of this year, it didn't dip. In fact, it kind of increased, and now we've fallen off a map in October," mentioned Manus Clancy, head of data strategy at LightBox. "It's like we've reached this straw that has broken the camel's back in terms of people saying, 'Okay, enough is enough. I can't keep putting money to work without some clarity on where interest rates are going.'".

    Clancy said deals were happening earlier this year because investors had gotten more comfortable with where interest rates had settled. The office market was beginning to recover as more companies ordered workers back. Multifamily, which had seen a glut of new construction, was also starting to see vacancies fall and rents rise.

    This takes the market back to 2023, when deal-making froze up because interest rates had shot up sharply from very low, pandemic-induced levels. As property values repriced, the gap between what the sellers wanted and what the buyers were willing to pay widened. That is what is happening now.

    "The wheels of progress just completely stop," said Clancy.

    Recent findings suggest that whether they are refinancing a loan or getting a fresh loan to purchase a property, investors, developers and property owners are now deciding to wait to see if interest rates come down at all. While the Federal Reserve is expected to raise its lending rate further, an end to the war with Iran could bring Treasury yields down. Especially for refinances, borrowers would be out millions of dollars at these higher rates. On the buy side, deals simply don't work anymore at higher rates.

    Sources indicate that "I think it is disorienting as people try to rebase values, and in the midst of transactions, you're seeing value retrades at the 11th hour, deals getting pulled, and volume slowing down yet again in the market," stated Ryan Cotton, head of real estate at Bain Capital in a recent Property Play podcast. "It's definitely a confusing and complicated time to be a real estate investor.".

    Higher interest rates were the leading factor for the slowdown in October, but LightBox cited another contributing factor. Lending remains open, but sentiment has weakened. It points to the Mortgage Bankers Association cutting its 2027 growth forecast for commercial mortgage lending from about 8% to 1%. In addition, the Commercial Real Estate Finance Council, or CREFC, Sentiment Index fell 17.5% in the third quarter of this year to a three-year low.

    Industry observers note that "People are lending for construction. They're lending for office conversion. They're lending for fresh purchases," noted Clancy. "We look at this index as kind of the tip of the spear. That if something's going to go sideways, this is the first indicator that people are stopping the ordering of appraisals, and we think that this portends that the next quarter will show a lot of decline in bank lending on commercial real estate.".

    CNBC's Property Play with Diana Olick covers latest and evolving opportunities for the real estate investor, delivered weekly to your inbox.

    #176526. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

    📅 05 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3254 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

    📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3254 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources.
    • It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.
    • “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

    It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

    “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

    “I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”.

    In a recent development, what a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

    Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

    According to recent reports, to say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

    It has been revealed that the warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

    The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

    And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

    It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

    Recent findings suggest that it promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”.

    Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

    “Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”.

    Gasly himself stated he had no idea what he was capable of. “My blueprint is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

    Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

    He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

    In a recent development, he told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”.

    Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”.

    Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

    “We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”.

    Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”.

    Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

    P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY.

    In a recent development, he indicates: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”.

    He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

    “I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

    According to recent reports, alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

    His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

    Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

    Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

    Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

    According to recent reports, he starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

    After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

    Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

    Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

    Piastri may be in for some bother.

    Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

    Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql.

    Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

    Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

    “**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

    Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

    Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

    There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

    The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs.

    But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

    Industry observers note that verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

    Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

    Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

    Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

    The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

    Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

    Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

    FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu.

    Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

    Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

    The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

    No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

    We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

    It has been revealed that 18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

    In a recent development, monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

    Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a significant opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

    The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2.

    The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

    There are actually times when affection for a car firm makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

    In a recent development, sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC.

    As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

    Recent findings suggest that the Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

    Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”.

    Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

    3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M.

    Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

    Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

    George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6.

    I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car firm, isn’t there?

    Recent findings suggest that 🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx.

    The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

    Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI.

    Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

    In a recent development, “Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

    ‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’.

    “Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

    Industry observers note that “What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”.

    He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

    Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

    Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

    Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft.

    The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

    Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

    With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

    Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

    The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

    Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

    A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM.

    The pair are just natural friends.

    Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT.

    The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

    “Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton stated yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

    “The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”.

    Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

    Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

    They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

    Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

    Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

    On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

    The full list of times from earlier today.

    FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT.

    Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

    Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

    He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

    “I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

    It has been revealed that “It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”.

    According to recent reports, russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

    According to recent reports, however, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

    Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

    Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

    According to recent reports, perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

    Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 04:01 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:06 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • Mauricio Pochettino has warned that Manchester United cannot be stuck in the past as he begins the job of dragging the biggest club in English football out of the Premier League relegation zone.
    • Pochettino faces a huge first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, and he is determined to make a fresh start at United uninhibited by the history of the club.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

    Published: 04:01 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:06 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Mauricio Pochettino has warned that Manchester United cannot be stuck in the past as he begins the job of dragging the biggest club in English football out of the Premier League relegation zone.

    Pochettino faces a huge first game in charge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, and he is determined to make a fresh start at United uninhibited by the history of the club.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy, in the way that we love to work. I think our job is to adapt and to go ahead a little bit,’ he stated at Carrington.

    According to recent reports, ‘The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear. It's an historic club with years being one of the best clubs in the world. It's difficult to find another club the size of Manchester United. It needs to be in a different place than we are now, no?

    According to recent reports, ‘But I don't think too much in the past. If we want to create something different and positive, and the people feel proud about that, it's about building our own way here. Thinking on what happened yesterday is not going to help. You cannot be stuck in the past.’.

    Pochettino’s appointment at United has been a whirlwind after the Argentine oversaw his final two games in charge of the US national team before flying through the night to start work on Wednesday.

    Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time as Man United boss on Friday.

    ‘I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool,’ he added.

    ‘My first target is to sleep, but I cannot sleep – only three or four hours per day – but I think the target is to know the people, the staff, all the people here in the club, and of course the players and try from the beginning to have a positive impact.’.

    Pochettino admits he has missed being involved in day-to-day coaching at club level, saying: ‘Of course, we missed it a lot. We are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we need to smell the grass and to help the players to improve every day.

    ‘It's true that it's a different job when you are in the national team, but I think we are much better coaches now.’.

    The 54-year-old told United that he wants to be involved in the all the key decision-making and transfers despite only being named as the club’s head coach.

    Pochettino demanded more control during his five years in charge of Tottenham, and the difference between manager and head coach has also been a bone of contention at United in recent years.

    Manchester United travel to rivals Liverpool on Sunday searching for their first league win since August.

    Ruben Amorim was sacked after taking on the United hierarchy over his job title, while Erik ten Hag refused to give up his power to veto transfers.

    Pochettino said: ‘I know that being a head coach, I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday and I'm going to pick the starting 11.

    In a recent development, ‘I'm going to make the changes and of course that, in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen in the squad. That is (why) in the end, Manchester United is a football club, no?

    ‘During all my (career), when I started at Espanyol, head coach, coach, manager. In the end, it's not changing too much because I think the way that we work is indifferent to the title description.

    It has been revealed that ‘If you are manager it’s not necessarily that you have all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and have more power in the decision.’.

    Pochettino revealed that he met most of the players individually at Carrington on Thursday, including captain Bruno Fernandes who cut a frustrated figure towards the end of Michael Carrick’s time in charge.

    Pochettino confirmed that out-of-form Bruno Fernandes will remain as United captain.

    ‘Bruno is our captain and I think he's a very notable player, but all the players need to feel that they are important from the top to the bottom,’ mentioned Pochettino.

    ‘Yesterday we spent three hours chatting in an individual way in my office with all the players.’.

    Concerns have been raised over the players’ fitness and attitude under Carrick this season, with the statistics suggesting that United have not been running enough.

    ‘That's a good question, no?,’ mentioned Pochettino. ‘It’s a debate that I don't like to go into because I think we cannot talk about things without context, and data is about context. I think it's very dangerous to talk. We are here not to denounce things, we are here to build something.’.

    Pochettino later shared a message on Instagram thanking supporters for their 'warm welcome' and declared the Red Devils 'cannot afford to waste a moment'.

    'An intense first few days. Thank you to everyone for a warm welcome,' the Argentine wrote.

    In a recent development, 'We cannot afford to waste a moment. All our energy and attention is focused on preparing for Sunday.

    'We can say many things, but what matters is the work we do and what we show on the pitch.'.

    Kushner-backed OakNorth secures U.S. bank charter as global digital banks push into America

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The U.K.'s OakNorth has secured a federal bank charter, saying it is the first foreign digital bank to do so, as international competitors vie for U.S.
    • The charter clears OakNorth, which is backed by Jared Kushner's private equity firm, to acquire Michigan-based Community Unity Bank, subject to an $80 million capital injection, according to approval documents issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Nov.
    • The deal, which is expected to close by the end of 2026, would allow OakNorth to provide loans, take deposits, and offer other banking services across all 50 states.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The U.K.'s OakNorth has secured a federal bank charter, saying it is the first foreign digital bank to do so, as international competitors vie for U.S. market share.

    The charter clears OakNorth, which is backed by Jared Kushner's private equity firm, to acquire Michigan-based Community Unity Bank, subject to an $80 million capital injection, according to approval documents issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Nov. 19.

    The deal, which is expected to close by the end of 2026, would allow OakNorth to provide loans, take deposits, and offer other banking services across all 50 states.

    Kushner's private equity firm, Affinity Partners, took an 8% stake in OakNorth in 2025, with backing from major Gulf investors, including the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia and Qatar. SoftBank is also an OakNorth investor.

    The bank reported $295 million in pretax profit for 2025 in its annual report, up from $280 million the previous year and close to three times the $100 million in profits five years prior.

    It mentioned principal losses on $20 billion in credit facilities issued over the past 10 years totaled £9 million, or less than 0.05%. Its 1.4% return on assets placed it among the top five banks in Western Europe and in the top 1% of commercial banks globally, according to The Banker's rankings.

    "I would say that the level of animal spirits in the U.S. is always higher, right? So the momentum of business and the optimism is always a step up," OakNorth CEO Rishi Khosla told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Monday.

    Recent findings suggest that he mentioned U.S. economic growth, investment in artificial intelligence and infrastructure spending would create opportunities for the bank.

    Recent findings suggest that oakNorth has focused on lending to lower mid-market businesses rather than competing for consumer customers in a crowded U.S. market.

    The lender targets businesses with annual revenues of $5 million to $100 million with loans worth $5 million to $50 million. The bank entered the U.S. market in 2023 and has lent about $3.5 billion to U.S. businesses to date. The U.S. accounted for 40% of its $12.4 billion in upcoming loans in 2025.

    "These are really growth companies which are scaling up, and given that focus, you really haven't had an institution in the last decades that focus on that customer segment, and that's opened up the opportunity for us," Khosla mentioned.

    He cited commercial real estate lending as a particularly strong growth opportunity in the U.S.

    In a recent development, securing the charter is notoriously difficult, with many regulatory hurdles. It took OakNorth 20 months, a restructure of the bank's corporate ownership, and relocating its holding company from the island of Jersey to the U.K. to meet Federal Reserve requirements.

    It has been revealed that other international fintechs seeking a foothold in the U.S. have struggled to gain traction. Monzo and Revolut withdrew their initial U.S. applications for a full banking charter between 2021 and 2023 after regulatory pushback.

    In a recent development, monzo closed its U.S. operations in April just four years after it rolled out, amid a crowded consumer market. "We have made a strategic decision to focus on scaling in our home market and Europe and to step away from the U.S.," the organization stated.

    According to recent reports, but the regulatory landscape has since shifted. Revolut and Brazil's Nubank have received conditional approval for U.S. banking charters from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

    Dutch digital bank Bunq reapplied after withdrawing its 2023 application, but its second application was denied in August.

    Another U.K. digital lender, Starling, is also seeking U.S. growth. It sells its Engine banking software to mid-tier U.S. lenders and is looking to acquire a domestic bank to serve business clients.

    • Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    Recent findings suggest that first, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout swiftly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    Zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One vital clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    From here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1099 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones stated directors did not intend to reinstate him.
    • Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.
    • According to recent reports, the reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the manufacturer reported strong third-quarter results.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang made a dramatic return as Nvidia CEO on Monday, less than a week after board Chairman Harvey Jones stated directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back.

    Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% during the session and closed 31% higher.

    According to recent reports, the reversal followed a steep decline in Nvidia shares, which closed at $125.53 on Friday even after the manufacturer reported strong third-quarter results. A petition calling for Huang's return had drawn more than 200,000 signatures, according to its organizers.

    The rally spread across the broader market, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 6.5% and the S&P 500 rising 4.7%, each posting its strongest session since April 2025.

    Nvidia's board said it had received input from senior U.S. government officials and that its investigation into Huang's conduct would continue.

    Still, the board's reversal, President Donald Trump's administration's role and continued scrutiny of Nvidia's China business leave major questions for both investors and lawmakers.

    Sources indicate that sen. Jack Reed, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, urged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Monday to appear before the committee to discuss the case.

    Reed did not lay out a specific list of questions for the two officials, but his statement cited reporting that Trump had been briefed by intelligence officials led by then-National Security Adviser Marco Rubio before intervening in support of Huang's return.

    Reed's call adds to mounting pressure on both Nvidia and the Trump administration to explain what they knew and when.

    Industry observers note that rep. Gabe Amo, D-R.I., vice ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, mentioned Huang’s reinstatement could broaden congressional scrutiny rather than bring it to a close.

    “I think it frankly broadens the scope of the query,” Amo told CNBC, adding that lawmakers should also examine administration officials involved in decisions affecting Nvidia and chip sales to China.

    Industry observers note that amo mentioned he expects the planned closed-door interview with Huang on Dec. 1 to proceed and that Congress would continue seeking answers both privately and publicly in the coming months.

    Recent findings suggest that “He should start purchasing his plane tickets to Washington,” he mentioned. “It is abundantly clear that this is ripe for questioning by Congress.”.

    Recent findings suggest that on Nvidia's third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 17, Jones noted the board had accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him.

    Less than a week later, the board reversed course, saying Monday that it had unanimously voted to bring Huang back after discussions with him and input from senior U.S. government officials.

    In a recent development, trump noted he had spoken with board members and that his administration provided assurances based on the information available to it. But the board has not publicly detailed what it was told.

    "The board decided to do what we wanted to do," Trump told CNBC, adding that he believed his intervention had been vital.

    "I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it," he said.

    Trump also called into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's return, Semafor reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

    Reed has called on Huang to disclose his communications with Trump and on Nvidia to release a transcript of the board's call with the president.

    Lawmakers are still seeking answers about the alleged smuggling of Nvidia products to China, their possible diversion for military use and possible advancement of Chinese AI capabilities.

    The Senate Banking Committee has scheduled Huang to testify on U.S. export controls on Dec. 3. House lawmakers have also confirmed closed-door interviews with Huang on Dec. 1 and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2.

    Industry observers note that "The Nvidia board's brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed," Reps. John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford and Brian Mast said in a joint statement.

    Their inquiry may also examine what Nvidia knew about the customers and resellers involved, as well as what controls the company had in place.

    Sources indicate that other lawmakers have also sought to preserve the paper trail. Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons had asked senior administration officials on Nov. 11 to retain records related to Nvidia exports of advanced AI chips to China and associated national security concerns.

    Nvidia has promised to hire a chief compliance officer and establish a committee overseeing national security and export controls. The board's investigation into Huang's conduct also remains underway.

    Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for APAC and the Middle East, said investors will be watching whether those new safeguards carry meaningful authority.

    Succession remains another question.

    In a recent development, gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, mentioned Nvidia has a limited window to prepare for the possibility that a future president may be less supportive of Huang.

    With Trump's term ending in two years, Luria argued that Nvidia needs a clearer plan for who could take over if Huang were forced to leave again.

    Gilbert pointed to Nvidia's roughly 75% revenue-growth forecast for the next financial year as evidence of strong near-term demand. The longer-term question, he remarked, is whether customer orders and artificial intelligence investment can sustain that pace.

    Luria told CNBC that concerns about the broader AI trade remain, including the cost of financing data centers, potential overbuilding by neocloud companies and obstacles to building new facilities.

    Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon said worries about whether AI spending is achievable and sustainable were not caused solely by Huang's departure. UBS, meanwhile, flagged Nvidia's roughly $390 billion in supply commitments and the need to keep demand flowing through its ecosystem.

    Industry observers note that gilbert said part of Monday's rally reflected investors recovering earlier losses rather than pricing in fresh growth. Bernstein restored its "Outperform" rating and kept its $200 price target, while UBS maintained its $220 target.

    "For the share price, it comes down to whether Nvidia can keep delivering as it has done over recent years," said Gilbert, adding that Huang's return could ease some concerns about Nvidia's longer-term outlook.

    It has been revealed that "The real worry has been what happens beyond next year. Having Huang back at the helm goes a long way to easing those concerns, because he's the one who sits down with the biggest customers and gets those multi-year orders over the line," he said.

    — CNBC's David Sucherman, Justin Papp and Eko Prasetyo contributed to the story.

    Latest Update: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

    📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4340 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that this was the definition of a hard-earned point.
    • According to recent reports, newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
    • Industry observers note that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that this was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

    According to recent reports, newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

    Industry observers note that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

    Recent findings suggest that ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

    For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

    “It reveals where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

    “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed massive character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

    In a recent development, A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

    But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

    In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

    It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

    When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

    It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

    That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

    On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

    Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

    Sources indicate that tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

    Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

    Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

    Industry observers note that justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

    Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

    Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

    Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

    Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

    That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

    Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

    The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under latest head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

    In a recent development, despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

    Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

    In a recent development, at opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

    Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

    Nvidia brought Jensen Huang back. But the investigations aren’t over

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (637 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang has the backing of U.S.
    • But investigations and governance questions still hang over the chipmaker, and analysts stated that internal and external probes of Huang and Nvidia could fuel uncertainty.
    • Industry observers note that trump's intervention to have Huang reinstated, alongside a concerted campaign from investors and employees, saw the Nvidia co-founder return just 11 days after he resigned amid reports of extramarital relationships, including one with a woman whom U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang has the backing of U.S. President Donald Trump and investors: Nvidia's stock gained nearly $1 trillion after the abrupt board reversal that reinstated him as CEO.

    But investigations and governance questions still hang over the chipmaker, and analysts stated that internal and external probes of Huang and Nvidia could fuel uncertainty.

    Industry observers note that trump's intervention to have Huang reinstated, alongside a concerted campaign from investors and employees, saw the Nvidia co-founder return just 11 days after he resigned amid reports of extramarital relationships, including one with a woman whom U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy.

    Shares rose 31% Monday and were around 5% lower in Tuesday's premarket trading.

    It was a dramatic turnaround just days after Nvidia's fresh board chair, Harvey Jones, rejected calls to reinstate Huang on Nov. 17.

    Nvidia, which had not responded to a CNBC request for comment as this article went live, is investigating reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, which the organization mentioned on Monday would continue as it restored him to the top job.

    California's Department of Justice is probing whether Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public.

    Industry observers note that reuters reported on Friday that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into the manufacturer's accounting practices. The SEC declined to comment.

    It has been revealed that huang is expected to appear before Congress twice in December, when lawmakers are set to ask about China's access to advanced Nvidia chips and U.S. export controls.

    Sebastien Naji, analyst at William Blair, stated in a note on Monday that Huang's return "clears some of the uncertainty" about the company but "events of recent weeks have exposed deeper questions around corporate governance, leadership succession, and regulatory oversight that could have lasting implications for the company's competitive position.".

    Trump told CNBC Monday that he personally intervened to speak with the board about reinstating Huang.

    The president posted on Truth Social on Monday that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    David O'Connor, senior research analyst at Piper Sandler, remarked in a note on Monday that Congress will "likely want their answers" from Huang but, given the U.S. government assurances on national security, "we don't think this will translate into anything meaningful to the stock.".

    The board's investigation is the "key risk" that remains, said Cody Acree, analyst at StoneX, in a note on Monday.

    He wrote that any conclusion that "confidential information was shared" or that compliance was compromised would "reopen the leadership question.".

    But Acree added that the board's reinstatement of Huang suggested it had "confidence in where the investigation is heading, and the government input it cited lowers the odds of an adverse finding.".

    But scrutiny could slow Nvidia's deal-making, Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at Questar Capital Partners, told CNBC's "Access Middle East" on Tuesday.

    He called Nvidia "kind of the central bank of the AI trade," adding: "With all the scrutiny they're going to be under, it's going to be very difficult for them to have the same level of deal-making capacity out there in the marketplace.".

    Stacy A. Rasgon, managing director at Bernstein, said in a note on Monday that the board faced "legitimate questions as to their judgment and process, which has to make one wonder how they come to their other notable decisions.".

    Democrats taking over Congress in January could keep Huang and Nvidia in the "crosshairs," Rasgon added.

    Members of Congress from both parties doubled down on their calls for investigations into the company, as they expressed anger at Huang's return.

    Tech Report: Drugmaker Insmed shares rally 14% after Sanofi agrees to buy it in pharma’s biggest deal in three years

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (552 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Insmed shares rallied 14% in morning trading Tuesday after Sanofi confirmed it would buy the smaller drugmaker for $41 billion, marking the largest pharma deal since 2023.
    • The proposed acquisition includes Insmed's portfolio of two commercialized respiratory drugs as well as its pipeline of experimental candidates.
    • It's a big bet by latest Sanofi CEO Belen Garijo, who took up the role in May to steer the tech giant through its upcoming patent cliff, when its blockbuster immunology drug Dupixent will face generic competition as patents expire.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Insmed shares rallied 14% in morning trading Tuesday after Sanofi confirmed it would buy the smaller drugmaker for $41 billion, marking the largest pharma deal since 2023.

    The proposed acquisition includes Insmed's portfolio of two commercialized respiratory drugs as well as its pipeline of experimental candidates. Sanofi will pay $175 per share in cash.

    It's a big bet by latest Sanofi CEO Belen Garijo, who took up the role in May to steer the tech giant through its upcoming patent cliff, when its blockbuster immunology drug Dupixent will face generic competition as patents expire.

    If closed, the transaction will be the biggest one the industry has seen since Pfizer bought Seagen for $43 billion in December 2023.

    Insmed shares rose 14.3% to roughly $170.40 in morning trading, while Sanofi stock climbed 8% in Paris.

    Barclays analysts called the deal a "breath of fresh air," significantly improving Sanofi's Dupixent patent expiry outlook by adding Insmed's established respiratory assets Brinsupri and Arikayce, plus a late-stage pipeline offering further potential upside.

    The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027 and be accretive to earnings by the end of 2028, Sanofi mentioned.

    Like much of the industry, Sanofi faces a revenue drop toward the end of the decade as top-selling drugs lose exclusivity and open up for generic drugmakers to compete.

    Global biopharma has experienced a sharp uptick in deals in 2026, as the sector is driven by looming patent cliffs, newly buoyant public markets and a race to beef up pipelines. Following a post-pandemic trough in 2022, M&A activity surged in 2025 and has accelerated into 2026.

    While companies develop fresh medicines in-house, acquiring them is often faster and has become the go-to strategy for large biopharma companies with strong cash flows and financial firepower. Investors are also calling for sustainable revenue growth as major drugs lose exclusivity.

    "Sanofi could offer a far more attractive investment opportunity given the significantly improved growth outlook," Barclays stated in a note early Tuesday.

    Sources indicate that formerly CEO at Merck KGaA, Garijo is facing pressure to find Sanofi's next growth driver. Her predecessor Paul Hudson stepped down earlier this year after the board chose not to renew his mandate, following a six-year reign during which his costly emphasis on R&D failed to deliver speedy results.

    The Insmed deal is a good strategic fit that will help soften the blow from Dupixent's expected 2031–32 loss of exclusivity, said Jefferies analysts.

    Insmed's medicines Brinsupri and Arikayce could add significant long-term revenue, with forecasts of $6.8 billion and $1.3 billion, respectively, in 2035, the analysts said. They see further potential upside if a settlement delays Dupixent's patent cliff, or if Brinsupri is included in Sanofi's alliance with Regeneron and positioned alongside Dupixent in respiratory diseases.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Consumers grew significantly more optimistic in November in the wake of the midterm elections, with a growing number of Americans now seeing improvement in the labor market and expecting inflation to cool.
    • The Conference Board survey released Tuesday highlighted improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3, up 11.4 points from October and much better than the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 92.2.
    • Industry observers note that confidence among Democrats and independent voters improved sharply, the Conference Board noted, while confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Consumers grew significantly more optimistic in November in the wake of the midterm elections, with a growing number of Americans now seeing improvement in the labor market and expecting inflation to cool.

    The Conference Board survey released Tuesday highlighted improvement across the board, with the headline confidence index jumping to 103.3, up 11.4 points from October and much better than the Dow Jones consensus forecast for 92.2.

    Industry observers note that confidence among Democrats and independent voters improved sharply, the Conference Board noted, while confidence among Republican respondents fell slightly. Still, confidence among Republicans remained the highest among the three groups.

    While respondents "continued to express frustration with high prices and rising costs," they also "cited hope for the general economy," noted Fergus McCormick, the board's senior economist for global indicators.

    The survey comes with the Federal Reserve continuing to try to bring down inflation, which has run above the central bank's 2% target for some 5½ years. The Fed is expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point when it meets again in two weeks.

    Despite the lingering worries about the cost of living — a centerpiece issue during the midterm — the survey's present situations and expectations indexes both posted strong gains. Inflation expectations for 12 months from now fell for the second straight month but remained high at 5.7%.

    The survey's closely watched gap between jobs considered "plentiful" versus "hard to get" widened to 12.4 percentage points. The "plentiful" side rose to 30.8% from 26.2% while "hard to get" fell to 18.4%, down 3 percentage points.

    Industry observers note that the survey results are the second in the past week to show that Americans are growing more optimistic about the economy. The University of Michigan's November survey, released Friday, demonstrated a 7.3% increase since October, with a similar partisan split.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
    • Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 04:54 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 13:58 EST, 20 November 2026.

    The drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session at Manchester United has removed the video from his YouTube account and apologised to the club.

    United suffered the embarrassing security breach on Pochettino’s first day as head coach after the 12-minute footage showing the Argentine and his staff working with the players at Carrington was posted online.

    The owner of the account called CC Overview, who is known only as Colin, justified the intrusion by saying that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

    United will have to apply to the Department of Transport if they want to close off the airspace to avoid more unwanted drones.

    CC Overview took the video down on Friday morning insisting that he was unaware of the significance of his actions.

    He also clarified that neither Liverpool – who are United’s opponents in Pochettino’s first game at Anfield on Sunday – nor any other club were involved in the filming.

    Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session was filmed by a drone and the operator has now apologised.

    The drone user, who is known only as Colin, stated he had not broken laws but apologised.

    United have declined to comment over the incident and it’s unclear if the club have made contact with him or involved Greater Manchester Police.

    His statement read: ‘I would like to speak about yesterday’s incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

    ‘My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.

    'I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

    ‘I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets.

    Recent findings suggest that 'I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match. I would also like to state that Liverpool Football club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday.

    ‘The video has been removed from my channel. I have spent the past four years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well received responsible videos. Thank you.’.

    United say they will not pursue legal action this time but will not hesitate to do so if it happens in the future.

    To stop drones legally flying over Carrington, it has emerged that the club would need to seek permission from the Government to restrict the airspace around the training ground.

    Footage of the session was captured close to Carrington and uploaded online.

    There are tight controls issued by the CAA and National Air Traffic Services over flying drones of different sizes, and a code of conduct related to how they are operated. It includes sharing photos and videos that could be ‘unfair’ to anyone.

    It states that drones over 250g should not be flown closer than 50 metres to people, and drones below that weight should not be flown over crowds.

    According to recent reports, the drone and model aircraft code also states that you must ‘keep at least 150m away from residential, recreational, commercial and industrial areas’. It lists sports facilities as a recreational area.

    There are also rules regarding privacy, which may well apply to United given that Pochettino and his players were preparing for a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday – arguably the biggest fixture in the English football calendar.

    Sources indicate that it states: ‘Drones users must always respect your privacy and not cause a nuisance. They must comply with the same privacy regulations as anyone who uses a camera or recording device.

    Man United installed signs in 2018 warning that the use of drones over Carrington was 'strictly prohibited' and would be reported for prosecution.

    According to recent reports, ‘If your drone or model aircraft is fitted with a camera or listening device, you must respect other people’s privacy whenever you use them. If you use these devices where people can expect privacy, such as inside their home or garden, you’re likely to be breaking data protection laws. Any photos or recordings you take may be covered by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

    ‘Let people know before you start recording or taking pictures. In some cases, this will be easy. For example, if you’re taking a photo of family and friends at a family barbecue. In other cases, this will be less practical, so you must be careful to respect everyone’s right to privacy.

    ‘Think before sharing photos and videos. Avoid sharing anything that could be unfair or harmful to anyone. Think carefully about who could see your photos and videos – especially before posting them on social media. Apply the same common-sense approach that you would with images or video recorded on a smartphone or digital camera.’.

    Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola was asked about the drone on Friday, saying: 'It shouldn't be legal. There is a reason why we train behind closed doors. It's not nice for any club.'.
