    • Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.
    • Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues.
    • According to recent reports, mendoza's first start came in one of the toughest possible matchups against the Seahawks in Week 10.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

    Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

    Chris Rodriguez Jr., RB, Jaguars.

    Antonio Williams, WR, Commanders.

    According to recent reports, mendoza's first start came in one of the toughest possible matchups against the Seahawks in Week 10. Unsurprisingly, he struggled in that contest, but there were signs of fantasy upside, including his six carries for 22 yards and a touchdown.

    This week, we got a better idea of what Mendoza could become for fantasy and the results were excellent. Even with Brock Bowers out of the lineup, Mendoza threw for 267 yards and three scores versus the Broncos, adding another 22 yards on the ground. That locks him in as a top-five fantasy QB on the week.

    The Browns aren't the most fantasy-friendly opponent and the Raiders have a bye in Week 14, but over the final month (including the fantasy playoffs) Mendoza has one of the five best schedules at his position with dates against the Chargers, Broncos, Titans and Cardinals. He's firmly in the high-end fantasy QB2 mix with low-end QB1 potential given his late season slate.

    Watson is also someone worth considering as a fantasy starter this week and beyond.

    Recent findings suggest that the Browns have one of the softest schedules the rest of the way, including the Raiders, Bengals, Falcons, Giants, Ravens and Colts. That stretch begins with a Raiders defense that's top-five in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

    Cleveland hasn't had many favorable opponents for Watson, but he finished as a top-10 weekly fantasy QB in the two games against easier defenses (Titans in Week 5, Texans in Week 10).

    You can expect that to happen at least a few more times given his rushing stats and the Browns' strong, young pass-catching corps of Denzel Boston, KC Conception and Harold Fannin Jr.

    Cam Ward is 52% rostered but would be the No. 1 QB add, if available.

    Industry observers note that J.J. McCarthy at IND (18% rostered).

    Joe Milton at DAL (7% rostered).

    Sam Darnold at SF (27% rostered).

    Geno Smith at MIA (18% rostered).

    Anthony Richardson Sr. vs. NYG (1% rostered).

    Recent findings suggest that baker Mayfield vs. CAR (20% rostered).

    Jacoby Brissett at HOU (21% rostered).

    Risky streaming options (if healthy).

    Sources indicate that justin Herbert vs. NE (48% rostered).

    According to recent reports, kyle McCord vs. NYJ (3% rostered).

    Tommy DeVito at LAC (1% rostered).

    Michael Penix Jr. at MIN (15% rostered).

    Desperation streaming options (if healthy).

    In a recent development, carson Beck vs. WAS (3% rostered).

    Desperation streaming options (if starter is out).

    Josh Johnson vs. WAS (2% rostered).

    DJ Uiagalelei vs. NE (0% rostered).

    Somehow Black remains available in over 50% of Yahoo leagues, despite my endless pleas for managers to stash him on their benches. I'm not including him on the Top-10 pickups list, but just know he would be my top add.

    In better matchups, Black has shown solid RB3/flex value while backing up Christian McCaffrey and if the veteran ever misses time we would see Black emerge as a top-10 fantasy option.

    If you need a real-life example of what Black could do if CMC were ever sidelined, just look at what happened with Emmett Johnson when Kenneth Walker III sat out the last two weeks. Don't let players with that kind of upside remain on the waiver wire.

    Bhayshul Tuten is one of the breakout stars of the 2026 season, but he's missed or been limited in several practices over the last few weeks. To his credit, the sophomore back has managed to suit up every week. Unfortunately, he missed time on Sunday while battling the injuries, leading to just a 43% snap share and 13 touches for 53 scoreless yards in the loss.

    If the Jaguars are serious about contending for a Super Bowl, they need their star runner healthy for the stretch run, which makes you wonder if they will ever give him a week off. This week's matchup with the Titans seems like the perfect opportunity to get Tuten some rest, since Jacksonville is 14.5-point favorites.

    In that scenario, Rodriguez would step into the lead role and be a potential fantasy RB1 given the opponents and likely positive game script.

    Sampson hasn't had the biggest stat lines since returning from injured reserve, but he has been productive with yardage totals 77, 69, 48 and 37 over the last four outings.

    More importantly, he out-snapped Quinshon Judkins in three straight outings, turning this backfield into a 50-50 committee.

    Without a Judkins injury, the ceiling is limited with Sampson, so keep your expectations in check. But he's definitely worth considering as an RB3/flex option.

    Industry observers note that even without Lamar Jackson, Hill has been productive over the last three games. The veteran pass-catcher has at least eight touches in each of those outings, while amassing 92 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 9, 38 yards and five receptions in Week 10, as well as a season-high 98 yards and a TD on Sunday.

    Derrick Henry cleared concussion protocol after the loss to the Panthers, so he should be fine for Week 12 barring any symptoms popping up over the next 24 hours. However, even with Henry starting, we've still seen Hill have a set role in the offense, with the duo splitting snaps fairly evenly over this three-game span.

    Jacoby Brissett has given Hill 12 targets during his two starts and that doesn't seem to be going away. Fantasy managers can target Hill as an RB3/flex with some upside thanks to his pass-catching and occasional big plays.

    If Barkley is right, then Shipley would only be a flex option thanks to a good matchup with the Cowboys. However, if Barkley ends up being held out on Thanksgiving, Shipley would become one of the top pickups of the week.

    If Jeremiyah Love isn't activated from IR, Knight has a chance to produce as a sneaky fantasy option in those matchups.

    Latest Update: The Preview: It's time for Hibs boss Reedijk to bring sunshine back to Leith

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 16:03 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 16:18 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • Hibernian supporters know all too well the dangers associated with getting one’s hopes up.
    • It’s a road they’ve been down time and time again, only to end up with that same familiar sickening feeling in the pit of their stomach at the end of it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 16:03 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 16:18 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Hibernian supporters know all too well the dangers associated with getting one’s hopes up.

    It’s a road they’ve been down time and time again, only to end up with that same familiar sickening feeling in the pit of their stomach at the end of it.

    Which is why any talk of the Edinburgh club experiencing some sort of mini-revival should quite rightly be taken with more than a large pinch of salt.

    Let’s not forget, at the start of the month, new boss Marink Reedijk had picked up a paltry point from his four games in charge since taking the reins from David Gray.

    Performances weren’t up to much either.

    A statement win over Hearts at Hampden to book their Premier Sports Cup final spot was backed up with an emphatic 4-0 dismantling of Aberdeen up at Pittodrie.

    Hibs manager Marink Reedijk is still searching for his first victory at Easter Road.

    According to recent reports, credit where it’s due, of course. Both victories were hard-earned and thoroughly deserved.

    But it’s important not to read too much in to either of them. Players going above and beyond in a derby clash should be a given, while the Dons appeared to have chucked it altogether under the stewardship of former manager Stephen Robinson long before Hibs turned up in the Granite City.

    The real test begins this weekend with the visit of Dundee United, as Reedijk’s men look to secure a first home Premiership win in over seven months.

    Recent findings suggest that the fans have been crying out for entertainment in Leith for far longer than that. In the latter days of Gray’s reign, the atmosphere at Easter Road was verging on toxic.

    Reedijk needs to change that, and now has two games against the Dundee clubs over the next four days to get the momentum swinging in the opposite direction.

    Continuing to get the best out of his midfield three will be key to that.

    Industry observers note that the reintroduction of Joe Newell to the starting XI has paid off big-time. Not so much in terms of the stats, but rather what he allows Miguel Chaiwa and Josh Mulligan to do.

    The former was linked with a move to Celtic over the summer, but looked miles off it in the early weeks of the campaign until Newell lined up alongside him.

    Chaiwa can be guilty of trying to carry out too many jobs in the middle of the park, but Newell’s calming influence has enabled him to stick to what he’s good at — namely breaking up the play and moving the ball on to his more creative team-mates in front of him.

    There’s no doubt the Zambian is at his best when he keeps things simple.

    Joe Newell has provided a calming influence in the middle of the park amid this upturn in form.

    According to recent reports, newell’s presence has also freed Mulligan to play further up the field rather than on the fringes of his own box, where he was popping up far too often a couple of months ago. He’s wasted back there.

    If he can add some more goals and assists to his name over the next few, there is every chance he can play himself in to the thoughts of Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli ahead of the next set of internationals.

    It should be an intriguing battle this afternoon in the engine room, with United boasting the most cohesive midfield group in the top flight with Dylan Tait, Lyall Cameron and Zidane Iqbal.

    Of course, even if Hibs deliver in that sense, it may count for very little if the guys at the top end of the pitch can’t do the business. The lack of cutting edge has been an ongoing concern. Four goals against Aberdeen doesn't change that.

    Owen Elding appears to be Reedijk’s preferred option in the central striker role, but while the young Irishman has shown flashes of his potential, he has offered little to suggest he can be relied upon to find the net on a consistent basis.

    Sources indicate that the problem is, can anyone? Record-signing Thibault Klidje may have opened his league account for the season against the Dons, however we’ve seen enough to know that he isn’t the answer.

    Ante Suto is in the same boat, while Stoke City loanee Nathan Lowe has struggled for both game time and form.

    Sources indicate that and as for Rabbi Matondo? Well, the wait goes on to see any real return on that investment. Early days, mind you.

    That Martin Boyle remains Hibs’ main goalscoring threat is troubling, especially given that the veteran can’t even be considered a nailed-on starter these days.

    According to recent reports, there are a significant number of players — across all areas of the park — fighting for their future at the club. Indeed, you would imagine Reedijk is counting down the days until January when he will look to freshen up the squad with guys more suited to his style.

    Lyall Cameron has been a key man behind Dundee United's surge up the Premiership table.

    Hibs should use today’s opponents as an example of how patience can pay off.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s fair to say that Jim Goodwin has never been Mr. Popular in and around Tannadice. Goodness knows why.

    Many fans were calling for his head as recently as the summer after failing to secure a top-six finish last term, but he is slowly but surely starting to win over his doubters.

    Make no mistake, this season presents a golden opportunity for United to seriously challenge for third spot.

    You never know what you’re going to get from Hearts on any given week, while this is very much uncharted territory for Falkirk.

    And let’s face it, nobody would expect the likes of Hibs, Aberdeen or Motherwell to claw themselves into contention.

    While everyone else tries to stumble their way through a period of transition, United’s consistency – both on and off the park – could prove to be the difference.

    #176422. Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

    📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4832 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
    • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
    • He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

    This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

    He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he remarked.

    Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

    You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

    "Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

    It has been revealed that given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

    That was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a latest manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

    Sources indicate that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

    The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

    In a recent development, playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

    There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

    Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

    However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

    It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

    That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

    Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

    Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

    So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

    Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

    Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

    Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil stated: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

    “We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

    It has been revealed that as for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

    But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

    With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

    It has been revealed that the draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

    The third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

    Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

    Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

    Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

    From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

    “I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” noted Willock after the match.

    It has been revealed that “100% [the competition is crucial], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a new coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a substantial game in keeping that momentum.”.

    "We noted at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

    Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

    Recent findings suggest that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

    The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

    "Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

    We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

    Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

    It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

    Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

    Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

    Recent findings suggest that willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

    We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

    Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

    Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

    A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

    Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

    Sources indicate that newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

    Recent findings suggest that finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

    You can hear the travelling fans now!

    Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

    Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

    Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

    Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

    The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

    According to recent reports, millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

    From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

    Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

    Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

    Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

    Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

    Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

    Double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

    Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

    We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

    Sources indicate that what colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

    According to recent reports, it’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

    Newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

    González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

    The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

    Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

    Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

    The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

    Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

    Scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

    Promising restart for the home side.

    Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

    Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

    The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

    Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

    Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

    Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

    And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

    Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

    In a recent development, millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

    In a recent development, the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

    The delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

    Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

    The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

    Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

    In a recent development, newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

    González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

    Millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

    Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

    That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

    According to recent reports, newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

    The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

    I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

    When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

    As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

    Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

    In a recent development, first piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

    Barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

    Wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

    Recent findings suggest that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

    Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

    Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

    Industry observers note that again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

    Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

    Sources indicate that murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

    González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

    Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

    Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

    In a recent development, newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

    Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

    In a recent development, fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

    Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

    Just a reminder of the teams starting today:.

    Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace.

    Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

    Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

    Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

    Recent findings suggest that the teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

    "We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8.

    We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

    Alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach claims has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

    Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

    Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

    Sources indicate that at the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

    You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

    The Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

    Peterborough United vs Barnsley (7.45pm).

    Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm).

    Manchester City vs Norwich City (7.30pm).

    *all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise.

    Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

    Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

    Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

    Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

    According to recent reports, bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

    Recent findings suggest that aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

    Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

    Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

    Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

    The visitors have arrived in south London.

    We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT.

    We’re bringing you the action from the pick of tonight’s EFL Cup games but there are also four games kicking off at 7.45pm:.

    Crystal Palace vs Middlesbrough.

    The Champions League also returns tonight and you can follow along with both our blogs:.

    Aston Villa are at the moment 3-1 up against Club Brugge in Belgium – follow the action here.

    Manchester City will face Porto at 8.00pm – our live blog has just gone live here with the team news from both sides.

    Here is how the visitors are lining up:.

    Yoane Wissa takes the captain’s armband tonight, while Jacob Ramsey starts up front after scoring a late equaliser against Bournemouth on Saturday.

    Your Mags at Millwall ✊ pic.twitter.com/zfnHgTlWgh.

    Here is your Millwall starting XI:.

    Keeper Filip Marschall is making his debut while Jensen Metcalfe is back in the squad after his red card against Bolton was overturned on appeal.

    How your Lions line-up tonight 🔢 pic.twitter.com/wEp6qLIz4Y.

    Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

    According to recent reports, newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

    Recent findings suggest that alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the newly introduced season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

    Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

    Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

    But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Week 12 NFL slate has plenty of marquee matchups due to the Thanksgiving holiday. This year we have a Wednesday night "Thanksgiving Eve" game, the three Thanksgiving Day games and the third year of the Black Friday game as well. With games on three different weekdays, we are seeing some wrinkles in the calendar that we've never seen before.

    Sources indicate that the Packers are at the Rams on Wednesday night, and both teams are on nine days rest after a bye week in Week 11 into an early week game. The Thanksgiving teams all have three off days between games; on Friday, the Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers are teams with four rest days.

    There are no bye weeks this week, as all 32 teams are active. In the 16 scheduled games, only two of them feature teams that played last Sunday and will play this Sunday. This is the week of rest advantages and disadvantages, and hopefully there can be some angles to exploit where the market is not appropriately pricing these manual adjustments.

    Here are two early-week NFL Week 12 wagers I like right now.

    Using market ratings — a reverse engineering of the closing lines of previous games — to forecast upcoming lines, I would assume this line was Broncos -3.1. Normally, a 0.6-point gap is not that significant, but relative to the NFL key number of -3 — the most important number in sports betting — it certainly is. The manual adjustment worth making to this matchup given the schedule spot also has me downgrading the Steelers.

    Aaron Rodgers is the oldest active player in the NFL at 42 years old, and he plays the most notable position as a quarterback. But the age dilemma extends to other key players on the Steelers. Cameron Hayward, a star defensive lineman, is 37 and in his 16th season. Defensive back Jalen Ramsey is 32 and in his 11th season. Defensive end TJ Watt is also 32 and playing in his 10th season. The rest and recovery for these Steelers focal points presents a key disadvantage not present for the Broncos.

    While a veteran coaching staff is on both sides of the ball, this is only the second short week game for the Steelers under Mike McCarthy. The first was a Thursday Night Football loss to the Cleveland Browns. One-game sample sizes really don't matter much to me, but the approach and institutional knowledge of how to handle and what to expect on short weeks does. The game prep time is different, the practice schedule is different, the workout schedule changes, meetings for positional groups change, etc. There is a lot that goes into weekly prepping for an NFL game and the short week throws a wrench into formulaic aims.

    Denver is in its fourth season with Sean Payton as head coach and likely has a lot more foundational knowledge on how to handle these situations.

    I think the Broncos' game preparation will be sharper, and their bodies may be fresher. We also have seen Denver steadily improving while Pittsburgh has been regressing from its hot start. This week the first bet in for me was the Broncos moneyline.

    Industry observers note that the Colts will turn to newly-minted starting QB Anthony Richardson in this game after releasing Daniel Jones. The change sparked a lot of negative PR for the Colts organization, as they could have traded Jones at the trade deadline just a week before cutting him. Given the reports of the offers that came in, nothing was particularly moving and it's probably a negligible difference.

    Recent findings suggest that the one thing I still believe in for the Colts franchise is having a strong offensive mind leading the team in coach Shane Steichen. While he may not be with the franchise next year, he is very likely to get quickly rehired elsewhere because he is a great play-caller.

    With nine days off between games, the Colts made the QB change at the right time. This allows ample opportunity to prepare and install a friendly game proposal around Richardson's strengths. He is obviously very mobile, but what is most underestimated about his game is his arm strength.

    According to recent reports, steichen has already shown the ability to build a great offense around a similar archetype quarterback dating back to his days with the Eagles and a young Jalen Hurts. I think Richardson is going to be slinging this downfield far more often than Jones, and the chance for explosive plays by the Colts goes way up. This likely means faster drives than Jones, who would methodically try and plod the Colts offense down field before too frequently settling for a field goal. Explosive plays can generate instant touchdowns or scoring opportunities in a flash.

    On the Fresh York side, the run game has come full circle. The Giants struggled to identify their running back, benched Cam Skattebo for a game after a crucial fumble, tried to trade for reinforcements at the deadline and ultimately have gone back to Skattebo. Allowing backup QB Jameis Winston to run the team's tush-push QB sneaks has also proven incredibly effective. Malik Nabers has played himself into full health, and Isaiah Likely has fully blossomed into a huge receiving threat. The Giants offense is buzzing as well right now.

    I like the over in this game, as I believe the run game is peaking for the Giants, and the explosive play rate is going to jump for the Colts.

    #176413. Mauricio Pochettino must fix a club stuck in a constant cycle of failure. The new Man United boss has the personality but the squad is a mish-mash and where he sits as a coach is a great unknown, writes IAN LADYMAN

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1341 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

    Mauricio Pochettino must fix a club stuck in a constant cycle of failure. The new Man United boss has the personality but the squad is a mish-mash and where he sits as a coach is a great unknown, writes IAN LADYMAN

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1341 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 16:51 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:07 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • In a soft-focus Sky TV interview that followed Mauricio Pochettino’s opening press conference on Friday, the Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada revealed there had been a ‘buzz’ about the club since the arrival of their latest manager.
    • Whether he was speaking metaphorically or referring to the sound of drones stealing Pochettino’s training secrets from above only he will know.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

    Published: 16:51 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:07 EST, 20 November 2026.

    In a soft-focus Sky TV interview that followed Mauricio Pochettino’s opening press conference on Friday, the Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada revealed there had been a ‘buzz’ about the club since the arrival of their latest manager.

    Whether he was speaking metaphorically or referring to the sound of drones stealing Pochettino’s training secrets from above only he will know.

    As is usually the case these days, much about the modern United remains unclear.

    But what we do know after welcoming the eighth full-time manager since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson is that once again England’s biggest football club is relying on a personality lift to drag them back to their feet.

    According to recent reports, this is what happens when you get things wrong for so long, when you buy the wrong players and install executives who appear to be learning on the job. You end up hiring and firing managers, waiting for the one who finally arrives with the magic dust, the capacity to somehow create something greater than the sum of the rather wonky parts.

    Listening to Pochettino here – a talented coach and a good person – was to occasionally think back to words spoken in the weeks of their arrivals on this territory by predecessors such as Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag.

    For they too were asked about such intangibles as culture and mood and philosophy. They too were asked about more prosaic football matters such as match fitness.

    It’s a conversational cycle that tells a story of recurring and systematic football failure.

    Mauricio Pochettino faced reporters in his first press conference as Manchester United boss on Friday.

    A drone captured footage of Pochettino's first training session on Thursday.

    Amorim – back on a grim, foggy day exactly two years ago – was asked about Marcus Rashford and whether he had been right to spend time off in New York days before the new United manager walked through the door.

    Here, Pochettino could justifiably have been asked about another forward Bryan Mbeumo spending the wee hours of Thursday morning playing the newly released Grand Theft Auto video game when he probably should have been asleep.

    This is the United that Pochettino is now being asked to fix, a club where names and faces change but problems remain the same.

    The Berrada interview was actually more enlightening than Pochettino’s carefully managed introduction to the wider media.

    It has been revealed that certainly it was interesting to listen to his assertion that nine defensive players in one squad was enough. In football, as United are discovering yet again, it’s not necessarily the quantity that matters but the quality.

    One point did resonate rather more deeply, though, and that was the one Berrada – once of Manchester City – made about United’s players needing a manager capable of dealing with the scrutiny of the club and who could shield some of his players from all that comes with it.

    The recently-departed Michael Carrick did look rather lost on the touchline in the final tumultuous weeks of his time as manager. He didn’t look an awful lot more comfortable in front of the TV cameras either.

    Bryan Mbeumo posted this picture after the midnight release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

    According to recent reports, in the dressing room? Well, he lost the loyalty of his captain Bruno Fernandes towards the end and that is never a good sign.

    Pochettino will do rather better at all that. The former Chelsea, PSG and Tottenham manager has a personality and a charisma that could fill an aircraft hangar. His players will arrive at Anfield for his opening game on Sunday feeling better about themselves than they have for some time.

    United have hired some confidence and some authority and some experience at a time when they desperately need it, even if Berrada’s claim that they had to call the USA Federation last week to check on his release clause suggested this is an appointment made rather on the hoof.

    It is, however, the impact that Pochettino can bring over time on a jumbled squad put together for six different managers over an incredible 12 years that will define him. Here, the 54-year-old undoubtedly faces challenges.

    Talking this week to someone associated with Tottenham about Pochettino’s progressive seasons there between 2014 and 2019, I was reminded of the quality that the Argentinian was given to work with.

    Pochettino's Spurs side harnessed the attacking power of stars including Harry Kane and Heung-min Son.

    The French international goalkeeper, Hugo Lloris, the Belgian central defensive partnership of Toby Alderweireld and Jan Vertonghen, England international defenders Kyle Walker, Danny Rose and Kieran Trippier and, further forward, the burgeoning attacking talents of Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, Heung-min Son and Harry Kane.

    It has been revealed that it was a prototype Premier League football team, both in talent, age, fitness and physicality. That was why, in 2016, it almost won it.

    Industry observers note that pochettino does not have this at Old Trafford. He doesn’t have anything like it. He has some talented players. The fact he inherits a team in the bottom three is down to Carrick’s inadequacies.

    But this United squad is a mish-mash and it serves a purpose to ask how many would get in that old Spurs team we talk about.

    Fernandes? Maybe. Mbeumo? Probably. That is about it and that, frankly, is where United are right now.

    Pochettino has long wanted this job. It’s not a posting of convenience for him. Like others before him – men like Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal – he has long since coveted the cachet, the stature and the power of this remarkable football institution.

    Mourinho and Van Gaal had better players than Pochettino is being handed and they both still failed, largely because they were shown to be coaches already over the top of that hill that both had worked so desperately hard to climb.

    Mbeumo is one of the few United players who might have got into Pochettino's Spurs side.

    Recent findings suggest that where does Pochettino sit in terms of his own personal and professional growth? That is such a hard question to answer and will be utterly fundamental to how he travels in the weeks and months to come.

    Sitting here fresh from the training ground and strangely seeming to question whether the glass of water in front of him was fit to drink, Pochettino declared himself to be in his coaching prime.

    ‘I am a much better coach now,’ he remarked.

    Sources indicate that the proof or otherwise of that will only be revealed out on the grass. For all that he can plead valid mitigation, Pochettino was not hugely impressive in Paris or at Stamford Bridge. Before he starts to talk about dysfunctional football clubs, he may wish to take a look at his new surroundings.

    In a recent development, liverpool away feels like something of a free hit. Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday less so and Brentford at home next Saturday definitely not. And so it begins. A run of 12 games in six and a half weeks that may well see Pochettino crawling into January begging for fresh legs and fresh players.

    The newly introduced manager said here that he wishes to be across transfers and little wonder. When he looks at the mistakes made in that regard by a succession of United regimes and executives, he may indeed question what it is they put in the water in the north-west.

    United fans will perhaps appreciate that one of the ‘higher ups’ at Old Trafford has finally put his head above the parapet, even if they question some of what Berrada said. That’s been overdue.

    Recent findings suggest that in terms of their new manager, they can be forgiven for keeping a lid on any excitement. Many of them have simply been wearied by the cycle.

    NFL Week 12 betting: 5 biggest storylines, including Thanksgiving week spreads

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Home-field advantage hadn't really shown itself often during this NFL season, but Week 11 corrected that.
    • In a recent development, home teams were great in Week 11.
    • Here are the five biggest betting storylines for Week 12 of the NFL season:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Home-field advantage hadn't really shown itself often during this NFL season, but Week 11 corrected that.

    In a recent development, home teams were great in Week 11. Washington's win straight up and against the spread on Monday night meant home teams won 11 of 12 games (that doesn't count Sunday night's neutral-site game at Mexico City). The Chargers were the only home team to lose. Home teams went 9-3 against the spread as well. Before Week 11, home teams were just 72-78-1 according to Covers.com. After a massive Week 11, home teams are now above .500 for the season.

    Here are the five biggest betting storylines for Week 12 of the NFL season:.

    The Rams are favored over the Packers, but there's some skepticism about them baked into the line.

    According to recent reports, los Angeles is a 2.5-point favorite for its Wednesday game against Green Bay. Oddsmakers didn't want to have the Rams laying a full field goal, and it's understandable. The Rams are without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, which severely limits the passing game. The Packers also get edge rusher Micah Parsons, who tore his ACL last December, in the lineup for the first time this season. It's a huge game in the NFC wild-card race. Heading into the game, the Rams are -130 to miss the playoffs at BetMGM.

    Matthew Stafford of the Los Angeles Rams last faced the Packers in 2024. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images).

    According to recent reports, the Chicago Bears are a hot team, especially in the betting market. It's rare to see an 8-2 team be an underdog at home, but that's the case for the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving. The Bears are 2.5-point favorites for the first game on Thursday. That's not a lot of respect for the Lions.

    Sources indicate that that's a surprising contrast with the NFC North odds. The Lions are favored at most sportsbooks to take the division. That's mostly due to remaining strength of schedule. The Bears have the third-toughest remaining schedule, via DVOA. The Lions' remaining schedule is the 11th easiest. Still, if the Bears can win on Thursday, it would give them a nice one-game lead in the division with a leg up on clinching the head-to-head tiebreaker.

    According to recent reports, the Kansas City Chiefs aren't underdogs often, but oddsmakers had little choice this week. In the third Thanksgiving game, the Chiefs travel to face the Buffalo Bills. The Bills are one of the NFL's top two teams, along with the 49ers, and at 9-1 they had to be favored. And it's not a surprise that at most sportsbooks the Bills are full field-goal favorites at -3.

    Industry observers note that it is the third time the Chiefs have been underdogs this season. They were underdogs at the Seahawks and at the Broncos, and lost both games. They didn't cover the spread in either game.

    It has been revealed that for the record, the other Thanksgiving game has a spread of Dallas -8.5 vs. Philadelphia. Four of five good matchups for the weekday games isn't a bad rate.

    Recent findings suggest that since the NFL introduced a game the day after Thanksgiving, they have mostly been throwaway matchups. This season it's between two teams that would be in the playoff field if the season ended now.

    Sources indicate that the Denver Broncos travel to face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday. The Broncos are 2.5-point road favorites, which is a reflection of how bad Pittsburgh has looked the last two weeks. They were blown out by the Bengals and lost to the Eagles on Sunday as a 3.5-point favorite.

    While it could be a close game, oddsmakers don't expect it to be a high-scoring one. The total of 37.5 is the second-lowest of the week, with the Patriots-Chargers game at 35.5 coming in lower.

    Week 11 had five double-digit spreads. And the big favorites covered in four of those five games, with the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints being the only time a double-digit underdog covered.

    Industry observers note that this week there aren't so many major spreads. Jacksonville is a 14.5-point favorite against the Titans, the Bengals are 10-point favorites over the Saints and that's it for double-digit spreads. Eagles-Cowboys is the only other spread of more than 7.5 points. It's a better week of matchups around the NFL.

    Roberto De Zerbi defends Mykhailo Mudryk after on-loan star angered Spurs fans with interview gaffes - including admitting he wanted to join Arsenal

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1159 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • Mykhailo Mudryk is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.
    • Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

    Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Mykhailo Mudryk is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

    Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

    He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

    And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

    'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' mentioned Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

    'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'.

    Mykhailo Mudryk admitted he joined Tottenham to regain fitness before returning to Chelsea, while also stating he had wanted to sign for Arsenal in 2023 before his transfer to the Blues.

    Roberto De Zerbi acknowledged Tottenham fans' views on Mudryk's comments, but insisted the winger has 'suffered a lot' following his doping ban.

    Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

    Recent findings suggest that 'He has no responsibility in this part,' said De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

    'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'.

    Industry observers note that mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

    Recent findings suggest that 'The blueprint was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' said De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'.

    James Maddison's limited involvement for Tottenham relates to a niggling hip injury dating back to pre-season.

    Maddison has been an unused sub in two Spurs games since limping off when the problem flared up at Chelsea, on his second start of the season and his second start in six days.

    Roberto De Zerbi confirmed ahead of Saturday's game against Ipswich that it had been the same problem which dogged Maddison through the summer as he fought back from a serious knee injury.

    The Spurs boss revealed how his physical condition had suffered from not training regularly and reminded the 29-year-old England midfielder he could only make an impact in the Premier League in peak condition.

    De Zerbi confirmed James Maddison is available to face Ipswich but stressed the midfielder needs to push himself to reach his peak physical condition.

    'It is not a big injury, but he was not able to work,' explained De Zerbi. 'He had a problem with his hip. The same as preseason. It's not a big problem but if you don't work consistently you lose the physical condition and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.'.

    According to recent reports, maddison, who turns 30 on Monday, missed most of last season with a cruciate knee injury and has played only 195 minutes this season. His return was further complicated by a shoulder injury after coming on at Brentford on the opening game of the season.

    Recent findings suggest that 'He is still young, 29 years is not old,' stated De Zerbi. 'He has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.'.

    Maddison and Destiny Udogie have both trained fully through the international break and are available to face Ipswich.

    'He worked very well from the Wednesday after Leeds,' stated De Zerbi. 'From Chelsea to the Leeds game, he worked just three times on the pitch at the training ground.

    Recent findings suggest that 'If you don't work during the week you risk injury and lose the normal physical condition you need to play Premier League. The same for Udogie. When they work and are fit to work, they have many chances to play, especially Maddison because a special player.'.

    Sources indicate that maddison's first start of the season came against Coventry when he scored the opener and inspired Spurs to their first win. He barely trained but started again in the win at Chelsea five days later, where he broke down early in the second half and was replaced by Conor Gallagher.

    De Zerbi made it clear there were no problems connected to Maddison being pictured out at a pub in Coventry after the defeat at Leeds. It was the last game before the international break and the first of three days off.

    'I am angry because next time he has to invite me,' joked the Spurs boss and he added: 'I am happy. I know when my players work well. If they are serious on the pitch, off the pitch they can do what they want. I'm not a policeman.

    'James is top professional, top guy, top player. The private life is not our problem if they work well and they are serious, and give their best for the club, the shirt and the fans, and he is perfect when it comes to that.'.

    Latest Update: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

    📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
    • So much for the upcoming group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
    • And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

    So much for the upcoming group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

    And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

    Sources indicate that they can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

    “It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

    City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

    NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

    It has been revealed that there is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a fresh City, different personnel and even a new look.

    In a recent development, they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

    The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

    “I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

    Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

    Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

    Industry observers note that phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are upcoming to City’s challenge.

    That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

    Sources indicate that bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

    Sources indicate that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This reveals how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

    Sources indicate that by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

    Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he revealed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

    Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

    City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

    Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

    It has been revealed that man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

    But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

    “It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland remarked. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

    For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

    Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

    September 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City (Premier League)September 17: Manchester City vs Norwich (League Cup)September 20: Manchester City vs Sunderland (Premier League)October 11: Liverpool vs Manchester City (Premier League)October 14: Manchester City vs PSG (Champions League).

    Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig.

    “I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

    Recent findings suggest that 36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh.

    In a recent development, “I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a latest step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

    5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm.

    “Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

    “He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.
