    The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

    Recent findings suggest that enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

    Industry observers note that it has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

    Enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

    Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

    There will be five added minutes.

    It has been revealed that that is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

    Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

    Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

    Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

    Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

    It has been revealed that A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

    In a recent development, whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

    Sources indicate that that is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

    Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

    Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

    Sources indicate that porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

    For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

    Recent findings suggest that man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

    Ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

    Industry observers note that A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

    Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

    Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

    Industry observers note that varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

    That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

    Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

    In a recent development, just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

    It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

    It has been revealed that enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

    In a recent development, manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

    In a recent development, “It is a hard place to come [Porto],” stated Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

    Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

    In a recent development, “We are going to face one of the major favourites to win the competition,” Farioli noted. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

    Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're past the point in the fantasy football season where we can afford to be patient. It's playoff crunch time, and for a lot of fantasy managers, every lineup decision over the next few weeks could be the difference between making the postseason and watching from the sideline.

    Recent findings suggest that there's no time to sit around waiting for players to figure it out. We need production, and we need it now.

    Let's get into the Week 12 Panic Meter.

    According to recent reports, I know the noise around Kenneth Walker III is loud right now. Rookie Emmett Johnson has been sensational in the games Walker has missed, and fantasy managers are wondering if we're witnessing a changing of the guard in Kansas City.

    Recent findings suggest that the word out of Kansas City on Monday, via Eric Bieniemy, is that Walker remains the starter when he's available. When K9 is on the field, K9 is the lead ball-carrier in this offense.

    In a recent development, that "when he's available" part matters, though. Walker was listed as a non-participant on Monday's estimated practice report with a groin injury. Keep an eye on his status heading into Week 12 on Thursday night against the Bills.

    Here's what I will say: Johnson has earned a meaningful role in this offense. Think of him as a souped-up, "Super Saiyan" version of Jerick McKinnon. He deserves to be on the field, and his involvement shouldn't disappear when Walker returns. I can absolutely see Johnson settling into an 8-to-12-touch-per-game role, which could take something off Walker's ceiling.

    In a recent development, but the way this Chiefs offense is humming right now, both on the ground and through the air, there's room for both backs to be productive. When Walker gets healthy, this has a chance to be one of the best backfields in the NFL, if not THE best.

    If Walker is healthy and active, he's in your lineup. Don't let Johnson's emergence talk you out of starting K9. Also, don't let Walker being active deter you from flexing Johnson.

    Panic level: No Panic (for me)/Total Panic (if you're still a believer).

    It has been revealed that emeka Egbuka has now gone 16 consecutive appearances without reaching 65 receiving yards, dating back to last season. He's seen five targets in each of his last two games, totaling 56 receiving yards. Meanwhile, rookie Ted Hurst III just found the end zone twice for Tampa Bay.

    This is a far cry from the receiver who lit up the first half of his rookie season.

    In a recent development, so why am I not panicking? Because I've already adjusted my expectations. Egbuka isn't a WR1 or even a high-end WR2 at this point. He's a WR3 with the potential to deliver WR2 or WR1 production in any given week. If that's how you're valuing him, nothing from Week 11 should shock you.

    No panic doesn't mean he's a must-start. He's a WR3 or flex option, and there are going to be weeks when you have better options on your roster.

    Now, if you're still holding onto the version of Egbuka we saw during the first half of his rookie year, you should be in total panic territory.

    Recent findings suggest that sixteen appearances isn't a slump anymore. That's who he's been.

    Panic level: Some Panic (bordering on Total).

    Trey McBride probably belongs in total panic territory, but the sheer volume of opportunities he's getting makes it difficult to put him there.

    According to recent reports, the Cardinals are down to their fourth-string quarterback in journeyman Josh Johnson. There was legitimate concern about what that would look like against Kansas City on Sunday, but McBride still managed to draw a season-high 14 targets, turning them into nine receptions for 54 yards.

    Sources indicate that fourteen targets for 54 yards. That's where the concern lies.

    There isn't much happening downfield for McBride in this version of the Arizona offense. It's to get the ball in his hands as quickly as possible and hope he can make something happen after the catch. Touchdown opportunities are going to be difficult to come by, and the Cardinals still haven't settled on who will start at quarterback moving forward.

    The volume is enough to keep McBride in your lineup, but expecting him to provide the type of positional advantage we've become accustomed to is probably unrealistic right now.

    It has been revealed that close to total panic? Absolutely. Am I recommending that you bench Trey McBride in a 1-TE league? No.

    It wouldn't be a Panic Meter without a Latest York Jets player, and unfortunately, we have to talk about Garrett Wilson once again.

    It has been revealed that at the start of the year, I thought this would be the season Wilson finally got north of 15 half-PPR points per game. Instead, we're looking at another season in that 13-14-point-per-game range.

    In a recent development, this isn't a talent issue. We may have seen the best version of the Jets offense on Sunday, and that's exactly the problem for Wilson's fantasy outlook.

    Breece Hall and Braelon Allen combined for 36 carries and 161 rushing yards. Geno Smith was incredibly efficient when asked to throw the football, completing 17-of-21 passes with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Wilson played 90% of the offensive snaps and was still the team's leading receiver.

    Wilson's involvement isn't the issue. There just aren't enough passing opportunities when the Jets are leaning on what I consider one of the best 1-2 punches at running back in the NFL.

    If the Jets can run the football effectively, limit what they're asking Geno to do and capitalize on his passing opportunities, why would they change that?

    It works for the Jets. It caps Wilson.

    He's still an every-week fantasy starter for most managers, but he's a WR2 with upside rather than the high-end WR1 many of us hoped he would become this season.

    Industry observers note that after sleepwalking through much of the season, the Indianapolis Colts finally did what a lot of fantasy managers wanted to do weeks ago. They'd had enough of Daniel Jones, released him and handed the keys to Anthony Richardson Sr.

    Does that make this offense better? Probably not.

    Richardson hasn't proven that he's the answer to the Colts' passing game, and he's stepping into an offense that's already without two notable pieces.

    No Josh Downs. No Quenton Nelson. No Daniel Jones. No problem, right?

    In a recent development, where things could improve is in the running game. Richardson's ability to keep the football on read-option plays gives opposing defenses something else to account for and could open up rushing lanes for Jonathan Taylor. Of course, that same rushing ability could also cost Taylor carries and touchdown opportunities around the goal line.

    Taylor and Tyler Warren aren't necessarily in the same situation, though.

    Recent findings suggest that taylor's workload had been declining as rookie Seth McGowan earned more opportunities. McGowan's hamstring injury could push some of that volume back in Taylor's direction, although we don't have a clear timeline for McGowan's return.

    Industry observers note that JT has been borderline unplayable lately and continues to slide down my weekly rankings. There is at least a realistic path for him to get back on track if the volume returns and Richardson's presence helps the rushing attack.

    It's much more difficult to see that path for Warren. In four games since returning from injury, Warren has caught 11 of 25 targets for 85 yards.

    Maybe Richardson has been sitting on the bench all this time thinking, "When I get my opportunity, I've got to get the ball to Tyler Warren.".

    That's blind hope, faith and optimism at this point.

    Warren is going to be outside my top-15 tight ends for Week 12. If there's a dependable option on your bench or somebody available on the waiver wire, make that move.

    A quarterback change doesn't automatically fix a bad offense. Taylor has a path back to fantasy relevance through volume, but neither player deserves automatic consideration in your starting lineup right now.

    Welcome to the Coping Corner, Indianapolis.

    Latest Update: Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

    📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5491 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under fresh head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
    • On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
    • Recent findings suggest that so, earn it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under fresh head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

    On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a newly introduced contract.

    Recent findings suggest that so, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

    The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

    In a recent development, mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

    Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

    It has been revealed that there are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he indicated during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ fresh head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

    Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

    Sources indicate that for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A substantial European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

    According to recent reports, “I loved it,” Iraola remarked, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

    Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

    It has been revealed that as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

    Industry observers note that there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

    It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

    Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

    According to recent reports, we knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

    This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

    Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

    Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

    Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

    Industry observers note that the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

    Sources indicate that “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

    "You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

    September 12: Liverpool vs Fulham (Premier League)September 15: Liverpool vs Tottenham (League Cup)September 20: Bournemouth vs Liverpool (Premier League)October 11: Liverpool vs Manchester City (Premier League)October 14: LASK vs Liverpool (Champions League).

    "It's difficult to ask for more." 👏Andoni Iraola reflects on Liverpool's winning start to their Champions League campaign.🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vDH7bob0V8.

    Tonight: Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1 (home)October 14: LASK (away)October 20: Villarreal (home)November 4: Fenerbahce (away)November 25: Club Brugge (away)December 9: Porto (home)January 19: Inter Milan (away)January 27: Lens (home).

    Andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

    So far, four of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season have played on this opening matchday and all four have won:.

    Tuesday:Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3Porto 0 Manchester City 2.

    Tonight:Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Napoli 0 Arsenal 1.

    The final English club in action will be Manchester United tomorrow night, who host Azerbaijan newbies Sabah.

    According to recent reports, full-time scenes at Anfield as Andoni Iraola celebrates his first Champions League win as Liverpool boss! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/9XDUOprvS7.

    Barcelona 5 Feyenoord 1 Stuttgart 3 Viking 1 Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1 Napoli 0 Arsenal 1 PSG 6 Slovan Bratislava 1 Sporting 3 Galatasaray 1.

    Possession: Liverpool 45%-55% Atletico MadridShots: 14-9Shots on target: 5-4Corners: 7-5Touches in opposition box: 31-18.

    Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

    "We can achieve everything we want." 💪Dominik Szoboszlai full of belief after Liverpool's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid 👀🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ebSvagW4yx.

    There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

    Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ.

    It has been revealed that first Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b.

    Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

    That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

    Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

    There will be five added minutes.

    According to recent reports, liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

    Sources indicate that kerkez is at the moment down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

    Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

    The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

    It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

    Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

    According to recent reports, isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

    Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

    Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,.

    Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

    Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

    Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a fresh contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

    In a recent development, we’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The major challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

    The fresh Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

    According to recent reports, this is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

    Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on.

    Sources indicate that it is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

    It has been revealed that that is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

    Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

    Sources indicate that well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a upcoming contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

    Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

    Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

    Recent findings suggest that we are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

    Barcelona 5 Feyenoord 1 FTStuttgart 3 Viking 1 FTLiverpool 1 Atletico Madrid 1 HTNapoli 0 Arsenal 0 HTPSG 3 Slovan Bratislava 0 HTSporting 1 Galatasaray 1 HT.

    Possession: Liverpool 50%-50% Atletico MadridShots: 6-6Shots on target: 3-3Corners: 3-1Touches in opposition box: 17-3.

    Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

    It has been revealed that the first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

    One added minute at the end of this first half.

    There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

    “I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

    Recent findings suggest that liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

    Recent findings suggest that andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

    “I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola remarked. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a major challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

    “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a substantial responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

    Atletico Madrid presently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

    “We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone stated. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
    • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • Martin O'Neill will weigh up replacing Mika Baur in the Europa League squad after the midfielder was ruled out for up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

    Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Martin O'Neill will weigh up replacing Mika Baur in the Europa League squad after the midfielder was ruled out for up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury.

    The German hobbled off late on in Celtic's win over Kilmarnock almost a fortnight ago with a scan subsequently revealing that he sustained ligament damage.

    One of the Parkhead side's star men since signing from Paderborn in the summer, Baur's absence is a major blow for O'Neill ahead of a defining period in the season.

    While the manager will look to the likes of Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg to step up domestically, he will also consider using a UEFA rule to make a change to his European squad ahead of Thursday's match away to Torreense in Portugal.

    The rule allows clubs to make an alteration to the squad they submitted for the group stage if the injury is expected to sideline the player for more than 60 days from when it occurred.

    Van den Berg, Jota, Landon Emenalo and Shim Mheuka weren't on the original 25-man list so would be options to be drafted in.

    German midfielder Mika Baur could miss up to 10 weeks of action after injuring his ankle.

    'I would definitely check with the medical staff and Mika, for a start,' said O'Neill.

    Recent findings suggest that 'And speaking to him yesterday, he's really upbeat about it. Obviously, he will have that boot on for a few weeks.

    It has been revealed that 'I suppose deep down, if it was, let's say, 10 weeks, that's taking you right through to the end of January. I can't see us seeing him in the next six weeks.'.

    Baur's form following his £4.5million move has been good enough for him to win his first full cap for Germany after being called up by upcoming manager Jurgen Klopp.

    'He was doing great for us,' added O'Neill. 'It is a blow. And it seemed so innocuous at the time.

    'I thought that he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he'd landed on. It's just gone over. It's a real shame. He was playing great for us.

    'There's things that he can't do for a while.'.

    O'Neill revealed that Benjamin Nygren is also an injury doubt for Saturday's match with St Mirren.

    In a recent development, 'He didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning,' he explained. 'He's got a sore heel. He missed out the second game in Sweden's run.

    'He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks, so we'll see how he is tomorrow.'.

    19-year-old summer signing Joel van den Berg could make his first Celtic outing this weekend.

    Van den Berg hasn't played for the first team since joining from PSV Eindhoven for £3.4m in the summer with an injury impeding his progress.

    But the 19-year-old could be in line for his first-team debut against the Buddies.

    'I had a little chat to him,' noted O'Neill. 'He trained this morning, he didn't train yesterday. We played a bounce game during the week, Tuesday against St Johnstone.

    'He played in that game, came off and he was definitely limping for a while. He had a couple of days' treatment.

    'In the overall scheme of things, whether it's tomorrow or in the next week or two, I'd hope to see him make his mark.

    'As I stated to him yesterday, "When you get in, it's really up to you".'.

    O'Neill anticipates a stern test from a St Mirren side who often have not picked up the positive results their performances have merited under Craig McLeish.

    'The overall job he's done has been terrific, really terrific,' noted the Celtic manager.

    'They're having a wee tough time at this minute, obviously, with results, but his overall contributions, I'd say it's been excellent.

    'There are some really fine coaches in Scotland, genuinely, and I don't want to sound patronising or sycophantic, but there are.

    'We were up against one two weeks ago against Kilmarnock [Neil McCann], so I've got a lot of time for those boys who are coming through and who, to my mind, are every bit as good of coaches as quite a number down south.'.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that my daughter retired from the military at the start of the season and came home to start her civilian life.
    • Well, until we started talking about the Thanksgiving menu.
    • According to recent reports, she hasn't been home for the holidays in the better part of a decade, so we're pulling out all the stops for Thursday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that my daughter retired from the military at the start of the season and came home to start her civilian life. We love having her back. Our sons are excited to hang out with their significant sister. My wife and I get an extra driver for the boys. Win-win.

    Well, until we started talking about the Thanksgiving menu.

    According to recent reports, she hasn't been home for the holidays in the better part of a decade, so we're pulling out all the stops for Thursday. I'll have at least two types of meat in the smoker. Multiple veggie dishes. Not to mention the family members coming over to spend time at the newly introduced house. Between tomorrow's game, the Thursday tripleheader and a Black Friday special, I'll probably get roped into so many conversations I'll only be able to watch the game in pieces.

    If your situation is anything like mine, here's one thing I'll be watching for in each game. If that's all you've got time to check before food's ready, you'll know what matters for your fantasy football lineups.

    I'm glad Green Bay got an extra week to reset after going up against the Vikings. Unlike Brock Purdy and the 49ers, Jordan Love didn't fare so well.

    In a recent development, to be fair, Love isn't the first to fall victim to DC Brian Flores' unit. Purdy is the only QB whose efficiency metrics improve with a bunch of purple in front of him. But what might be more concerning for the Packers is if the slump lingers into the next game. Because it wouldn't be the first time.

    (Photo by Chris Allen/Yahoo Sports).

    Five of the seven QBs with a game before and after facing Minnesota posted a lower EPA per dropback in their next game than their average before the matchup. Of course, you can poke holes in the narrative I'm suggesting. Daniel Jones, Tyler Shough and Malik Willis aren't world beaters. But Josh Allen posted his first game under 200 passing yards after getting pummeled by Minnesota in primetime (10 hits, season-high). Jared Goff was an outright disaster in Miami, notching his first game of '26 without a passing TD and his third with three or more sacks. Again, this is why the Packers bye couldn't have come at a better time, as the Rams have their own way of creating havoc for enemy QBs.

    Week 10 was just the second game where L.A. could feature the vaunted duo of Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald. Turning them loose against the Commanders and Cardinals seems like some sort of crime. But it paints a similar picture to Love's environment the last time we saw him.

    Time to Pressure (Weeks 10-11): 2.2, T-1st.

    The Rams put QBs in a bind, but not by sending the house on seemingly every snap. In their two games together, Garrett and Donald have combined for 14 quick pressures. Braden Fiske and Byron Young have four each, too. Meanwhile, on the backend, their secondary has allowed just four TDs over a six-game stretch. They're especially stingy on intermediate throws, giving up three or fewer receptions on attempts of that depth in all but one game.

    Josh Jacobs is still recovering. The offense will have to rely on Love's shoulder yet again. So, if you look up and see him struggling to connect with his receivers, or Matthew Golden having another ill-timed drop, just hope one connects for a TD and we can move on to Week 12.

    I talked about Chicago's lackluster start to the second half of their season on Sunday. In truth, the Bears defense was the real MVP. The runner-up was the Saints' first-quarter offense. They've scored a total of nine points in the first 15 minutes in 2026. But after Chicago mounted a multi-score lead, Tyler Shough found a rhythm.

    Drive #4: 7 (Plays), 80 (Net Yards), 3:47 (Drive Time).

    In a recent development, now, on the one hand, just three of these drives turned into points for Newly introduced Orleans. And only one resulted in a TD. But look at the number of plays run and the time Caleb Williams had to spend on the bench. Surprisingly, Chicago generated just one more first down on offense than the Saints (18 to 17). Its defensive success rate (57.7%) was actually worse than the Saints' (60.3%). If Shough could do that, think about what the Bears' upcoming opponent will do.

    Industry observers note that jared Goff blacked out against the Bucs. HC Todd Bowles blitzed him on 36.7% of his dropbacks. Goff didn't even take a sack while completing 7 of 11 attempts. Tampa's defensive front put Goff under duress 43.3% of the time, and that didn't faze him either. In fact, Sunday afternoon, given the stakes, was Goff's best performance when pressured since coming to Detroit.

    Success Rate (when pressured): 58.3%, Highest (of 17 games with +40% pressure rate).

    Pressure-to-Sack Ratio: 7.7%, 4th-lowest.

    In a recent development, OC Drew Petzing's game initiative was perfect. They attacked the seams of the Bucs' zone coverage for multiple chunk gains. With Jahmyr Gibbs stepping up to block DT Vita Vea, the Lions could flood the exterior of the defensive coverage with four receivers out on a route (2 WRs, 2 TEs) on 28.6% of Goff's dropbacks. Or, as the above clip highlights, he could beat them the old-fashioned way with Jameson Williams.

    Chicago just let the Saints dink-and-dunk their way into a close game. And the Lions can play that way, too. But the explosive element always lies in wait. So, if the Bears stall on either side of the ball, the Lions can pounce on them and maintain their lead in the NFC North.

    Sources indicate that I didn't turn on the PIT-PHI game until late in the fourth quarter. My thought was Pittsburgh would pull out the win, and the race in the AFC North would stay close. But on just 21 passing attempts, Joe Milton got his first win as a starting QB. But it wasn't all pretty.

    Recent findings suggest that to say the Eagles are trying to ease Milton into the role (i.e., hiding their passing game) would be kind. Philadelphia went from a -1.1% PROE in his first start, had the bye week to blueprint and came out throwing even less (-10.6%). Don't get me wrong — Milton didn't acquit himself of any poor play. He ranked second-worst and fifth-worst, respectively, in CPOE across both starts. Somehow, at 6'5"-246lbs., Milton is averaging five sacks a game. Luckily, he's using his speed as a runner (3.6 FPPG on the ground), but the arm talent could use a boost.

    (Photo by Chris Allen/Yahoo Sports).

    Only three QBs have squared off with the Cowboys and not walked away with one of their best efficiency marks of the season. Dallas even switched defensive coordinators, and it was still in the bottom 10 in defensive success rate. Admittedly, Cam Ward's TDs were unethical at best. But as a Bengals fan, expecting your offense to score 30+ is akin to thinking hope is a plan. However, with DeVonta Smith back, Dak Prescott might need to do just that.

    In a recent development, outside of Smith coming back to a laughable 57.1% target share, he also took 61.1% of the air yards. Milton tried him on throws of 25 and 53 air yards, but the two couldn't quite hook up. If I see that on Thursday, we're in for a wild ride on Thanksgiving.

    In a recent development, the Chiefs have two problems they'll (hopefully) solve on Thursday. Well, honestly, the glitch belongs to us fantasy managers. But Kansas City's offense does have something of a dilemma on its hands.

    Watching Emmett Johnson come in relief of Kenneth Walker has been great for both the Chiefs and fantasy managers. Nothing changed about how they do business. HC Andy Reid only opted to run on 46.7% of their early-down plays, but Johnson gained four or more yards on 53.8% of those carries. From a utilization standpoint, Walker and Johnson look interchangeable.

    Early-Down Rushing Share: 79.1% (Walker W1-9), 81.3% (Johnson W10-11).

    According to recent reports, but something has to give, assuming Walker is back from his groin injury. When both were healthy, the Chiefs ran six plays with both on the field. Mahomes is already averaging the 12th-most dropbacks per game, so there's little chance of Kansas City becoming a rushing team. However, if there's one area where the two RBs could split the workload, it's in the passing game.

    Yards per Route Run (as the starter): 1.80 (Johnson), 1.31 (Walker).

    In a recent development, it should be no surprise that the younger, faster rookie can churn out more yards with the ball in his hands and a clear runway. Regardless, if both are active, I'd expect to see more of a rotation between the two dynamic runners.

    However, the Chiefs' passing game has its own concerns.

    Recent findings suggest that I realize I'm going to come off as a Chiefs' hater, but the last two weeks have been preseason games for Patrick Mahomes. The last time he threw for more than 300 yards in back-to-back games was in 2023. Sure, the offensive line is still an glitch, but his hits and sacks have been down, too. And the timing couldn't be better, as it's allowed him to find the best ways to use his receivers.

    Industry observers note that HC Andy Reid hasn't unleashed Josh Downs yet. He was up to a 32.5% route share and five targets after making a splash in his debut. The good news for gamers rostering Downs is that when he was on the field, Mahomes was looking for him. His 38.5% TPRR led the Chiefs' pass-catchers. The downside is that on the eight routes that Downs wasn't the primary target, Mahomes was making magic with the other receivers.

    Industry observers note that the above clip highlights how No. 15 used Downs' gravity to pull defenders to the sticks, leaving space for Rashee Rice. Two plays later, instead of going to the intermediate part of the field again, Mahomes hits Emmett Johnson on a screen to set up an easy 4th and 1. The deep shots to Xavier Worthy or Cyrus Allen didn't always work, but the tendency to look 15+ air yards downfield hasn't been an element of the Chiefs' passing game for a while. And if Week 11 was any indication, Kansas City went from having limited reliable receivers to multiple.

    Travis Kelce: 18.9% (Target Rate).

    It has been revealed that in Week 10, six different pass-catchers earned three or more targets. That was up to seven against the Cardinals. Mahomes ranked 2nd and 9th in PROE in those games, respectively, but without a clear WR1, we're hoping someone other than the RBs gets into the end zone. That should change on Thursday night.

    According to recent reports, buffalo is first in offensive PPG and fourth in YPG. The Chiefs shouldn't have time to test things out or see what works best. Playoff seeding is on the line. So, I'll be seeing which pass-catchers become Mahomes' top options in one of the biggest games of the regular season.

    Recent findings suggest that I believed Jonah Coleman would take over the backfield in Denver. But I've been waiting for HC Sean Payton to do what he's done for years: split the backfield. Through the first six weeks, J.K. Dobbins played on 54.8% of the early-down snaps. But he was mostly off the field on third downs. Tyler Badie and RJ Harvey handled 77.8% of the RB touches in obvious passing situations. And everybody got the ball in the red zone. But maybe the rookie has made Payton change his ways.

    Thinking back on it, if there were ever a matchup for Coleman to take advantage of, it'd be against the Raiders. Their run defense was allowing a whopping 131.9 YPG to opposing RBs. And to make matters worse, the short-area coverage ranked 32nd in completion rate to rushers (91.7%). Essentially, any way that someone out of Denver's backfield got the ball, they'd turn it into a positive result. I just didn't think so many of those touches would go to Coleman.

    Short-Yardage Snap Rate: 100.0%.

    Going back to my thoughts on Payton's tendencies, how often he turned to Coleman isn't something we can wave away. His 88.9% share of the carries is the most of any running back since Payton came to Denver in '23. Third downs? All Coleman. Targets to RBs? 100.0% to Coleman.

    I have no doubt we'll see No. 20 start the game. But I'll be watching for his workload. And if we don't see any more Payton backfield hijinks, Coleman will have the OROY award locked up before the stores close.

    Can Celtic boss Martin O'Neill muddle through until January cavalry arrives?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
    • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.
    • Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

    Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

    Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.

    Since the first act of this season, a narrow win over Dundee, Martin O’Neill’s side have occupied a place of uncertainty.

    Those who have taken the occasional stellar display to be indicative of a corner being turned have been left feeling like fools.

    According to recent reports, there remain too many shortcomings in the squad, too many question marks hovering above too many players to ever feel that it has left inconsistency behind. The fan base has good reason not to quite trust it.

    How could it be otherwise when the clean sheet claimed against bottom side Killie was the first in seven matches?

    Kasper Hogh, the club’s record signing at £11million, hasn’t scored in his last 16 outings in green and white.

    Martin O'Neill admits it has taken longer than he'd have liked for the new recruits to settle.

    O’Neill’s options on the flanks include one player in Jota, who’s getting back from a long-term injury, and another in Yang Hyun-jun, who was recently sidelined for six weeks.

    There’s a veteran in James Forrest, Seb Tounekti, not exactly the bravest of souls, and Haissem Hassan, a £6m signing who evidently believes defensive work is optional.

    It states much that Callum Osmand, a centre-forward now trying to cut it on the flank, has become a fans’ favourite after just 13 senior appearances.

    The concerns of the manager now extend to the middle of the park where Mika Baur may be out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

    With Benjamin Nygren also a doubt to face St Mirren, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and/or Joel van den Berg could be teamed up with skipper Callum McGregor.

    We’re assuredly about to discover if this squad has more about it than the results and performances to this stage have suggested.

    ‘We can make big improvements, there’s no question about it,’ noted the manager.

    Industry observers note that ‘Top of the league, it is nice to be in that position. But other than a number of matches where I think we’ve played very, very well... maybe the Besiktas game, maybe the Hearts game, it’s been really hard work for us.

    Sources indicate that ‘That’s maybe a combination of things. Young and slightly more experienced players coming into the football club, getting to know the club, getting to know the players.

    ‘That’s taken a bit of time. I didn’t expect it to work immediately overnight.

    German midfielder Mika Baur is set to miss around 10 weeks with an ankle ligament injury.

    ‘But they’re at a club where settling in is something they’ve got to do pretty swiftly.’.

    Starting with the visit of the Paisley men, Celtic have 10 games up to and including the trip to Ibrox on January 3.

    That encompasses two assignments on the road in the Europa League — Torreense and Omonia Nicosia.

    O’Neill’s men also visit Tynecastle, Dens Park, Pittodrie and Tannadice in the league.

    As they prepare to put up the Christmas decorations on the Celtic Way, O’Neill could privately be forgiven for wishing the festive season away.

    January 5 is the day on which the transfer window in Scotland opens and you can’t help but wonder what Celtic’s prospects for the season will look like at that point.

    While Camilo Duran and Baur have contributed, the bulk of the business done in the summer again looks to have been sub-standard.

    To stand a chance of retaining the title, O’Neill badly needs several big-hitters to come in without delay in the Latest Year.

    Industry observers note that ‘We’re absolutely looking at players now,’ he stressed. ‘I suppose every single club is doing that. And the quicker you can get somebody in, the better.

    ‘We’ve seen when people are fit, we will have numbers. We just need a bit of quality.’.

    Camilo Duran has been one of very few summer arrivals to have made an impact at Celtic.

    Until such time as he can call for the cavalry, O’Neill has no choice but to make do and mend.

    On the chances of prioritising the league and playing a weakened side in Europe, the veteran is clear.

    Industry observers note that ‘Domestic football is really key to the football club, of course,’ he mentioned. ‘But you’d still want to try and make some show in Europe. And we’ve found that difficult.

    ‘I genuinely thought against Besiktas we did really fine in the game, we didn’t over-press because they could play through you.

    ‘There are certain moments even in domestic football when teams can play through you. Kilmarnock caused us plenty of problems.

    ‘I just think we’ve got to improve in the domestic games. We’ve got to be more aggressive in the sense of taking games to people and being less passive in periods of games.’.

    O’Neill clearly needs more — much more — from so many individuals if he’s to get through the shark-infested waters of the next six weeks unscathed.

    Hassan didn’t even make the matchday squad for Kilmarnock, a move which was interpreted by many as being a boot up the backside by a boss who’s been underwhelmed by his work without the ball.

    ‘We left out a number of players,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I wouldn’t read as much into that, because a few will come back.

    ‘My job is not to please everyone, otherwise we’d have 26 players playing at one time.

    O'Neill has backed misfiring striker Kasper Hogh to end his barren streak in front of goal.

    ‘I did a thing with corporate fans the other night, we had a bit of fun with some questions.

    ‘Apparently something came out that he [Hassan] was the most unpopular player in the dressing room, which is not true.

    According to recent reports, ‘I didn’t say this. I was joking about my own unpopularity, as a player, because all I did was moan.

    Industry observers note that ‘I did say about unpopularity, there’s at least one more unpopular. The crowd wanted to know but I didn’t tell them! I left it hanging. But it was tongue-in-cheek, apart from the part about me being unpopular, which I was.’.

    The form of Hogh is no laughing matter. The Dane looked the part when he claimed a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, but that is beginning to feel like ancient history.

    For his effort against the Ayrshiremen a fortnight ago to be ruled out for an earlier infringement by Baur was a low blow.

    Industry observers note that ‘For him, that was a killer,’ O’Neill reflected. ‘He has got the goal, gone off and celebrated and you just think... oh no, is that a goal?

    According to recent reports, ‘He has worked exceptionally hard for us. But strikers live by goals and at some stage or other, he needs a goal.

    ‘The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net.

    ‘Shaun Maloney was telling me that for a little period he played up front when Henrik was injured for about a month.

    ‘And Henrik in that time was giving him advice about how centre-halves were reading him. He told him about getting yourself room, losing the centre-half, don’t be fighting with him all the time.

    ‘He scored a bag full of goals, so there must be something in it.’.
